utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good morning to the parties, to all our staff, and to the public gallery. I would like to have some information, Mr. Petrusic, some information about General Krstic's health.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Yesterday afternoon and evening the Defence -- yesterday afternoon and evening, the Defence contacted General Krstic in the detention unit, and we understand that he has undergone surgery, so that he is now feeling quite well, but he is unable to attend the proceedings today. We have also been informed that the surgeon has made -- has scheduled a check-up for tomorrow probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: We are not having any new witness tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So he doesn't need to be disturbed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Please convey to him the best wishes of the Bench. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I think -- Ms. Krystal?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I just wanted to say: Last night we received by fax from the detention centre a waiver of General Krstic's presence here and the continuation of the hearing in his absence, so that will be brought up by the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you. I thought that waiver was already done yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It was for yesterday, but he also signed a waiver for today, and tomorrow, if in fact we go to tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In agreement with Judge Wald, we are not imposing hard and fast rules as far as the time is concerned, but it has to be within -- between 60 and 70 minutes, the session, so that you will not be interrupted when we have a cycle of coherent questions. So at least, but we should not have it less than 60 or more than 70. Is that all right with you, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Riad. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning Judge Wald, Judge Riad. Good morning, Witness DB. If Witness DB could be shown Prosecutor's Exhibit 827.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Harmon:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while Exhibit 827 is being collected, Witness DB, yesterday we were discussing the VRS intercept units that were focusing their attention on the enemy, and in that course of our discussion, we discussed the collection of intelligence data from outside the area of the Drina Corps. Now, the exhibit I'm going to show you is an example of an intelligence report of electronic surveillance that was collected by the East Bosnia Corps. And Witness, it may be of assistance to you if I give you my copy of the B/C/S, because I have highlighted certain portions that I am going to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: First, do Your Honours have a copy of this Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the upper left-hand corner of page 1 of this exhibit, you can see the identity of the group that sent this exhibit. This is the Eastern Bosnian Corps Command of the 3rd Radio Reconnaissance Platoon. And to locate us in space, the East Bosnian Corps Command was the corps that was immediately north of Zvornik, where most of the murders of Bosnian Muslim civilians occurred; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The date of this report is the 23rd of July, 1995. That can be seen in the upper left. And it is an intelligence report on electronic surveillance and it is directed to the Chief of Intelligence and Security of the Eastern Bosnian Corps. Now, this report shows the areas where the intelligence was collected, and one of those areas, one of the target areas identified is the Tuzla area. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you could move the exhibit up on the ELMO. I'm going to be focusing on Tuzla. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this information that was collected was information that was, among other things, tactical in nature. It was useful for finding and locating the members of the 28th Division who were attempting to flee from the Srebrenica enclave; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me read the first entry. It says, under the word Tuzla, "Some of the members of the 28th Division are hiding with their friends from the village of Kravica." And this is dated the 22nd of July. This information was intercepted at 1255 hours, and it was intercepted on Bosnian Muslim mobile communications. Let me go down two sentences. Do you have a comment, Witness DB?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says in the original that a part of the members are hiding at their friends' place from the village of Kravica. The translation I got was that they were hiding with their friends in Kravica, but in the original it says that they are hiding at their friends' place in the village of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, thank you for that correction. That's better yet. Let me turn to the next sentence, two sentences down: "Several groups of members of the 28th Division have set off for the village of Sapna." And further down it reads, "A report has been confirmed that several thousand refugees from Srebrenica are still hiding in the wider area of the village of Konjevic Polje. They cross over ARBH control territory at night. The ARBH Main Staff plans to launch a major operation to pull them out." Now, this was intercepted on the 22nd of July at 1850 hours on Muslim mobile communications. This is the kind of information that was conveyed to the intelligence section of the Drina Corps so the Drina Corps could analyse it and take whatever appropriate steps it deemed necessary; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let's turn over to the second page on the English version, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me read another portion of material that was intercepted. This time this was intercepted on the 22nd of July at 1750 hours off of the radio relay communications. "A person turned up in Tuzla saying that fleeing from Srebrenica he had been captured, brought before a firing squad, but managed to escape. He also said that the army of the Republika Srpska had so far executed by firing squad about 2500 persons from Srebrenica and its environs." Let me read on in this. Let's go down to the portion that says -- starts to describe the flight and the arrival in Kladanj of a group of soldiers, and I quote: "A large group of soldiers arrived in Kladanj from Zepa on the 22nd of July." And that intercept was the 23rd of -- I'm sorry, that information was captured on the 23rd of July at 9.15 in the morning on radio relay communications. Now, this Trial Chamber has seen a series of reports from the Drina Corps and from the Zvornik -- the Drina Brigade, I'm sorry, and the Zvornik Brigade of ambushes being set by VRS soldiers of Muslims fleeing from the Srebrenica enclave, and in part, it is our submission that those ambushes were set up based on intelligence information that was captured during the flight of the Muslims. Now, let me turn my attention now, Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm finished, Mr. Usher, with that exhibit, and if I could have my copy back. THE USHER: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me turn my attention back to Prosecutor's Exhibit 750, if I could have --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I make a comment on what you have just said?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you wish to contest the submission of the Prosecutor on that point? Do you wish to clarify the submission of the Prosecutor on that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am referring to some knowledge that I have and the knowledge that is probably by now in your possession, too. This report is dated the 23rd of July. According to actual developments on that day, I think that you have unquestionable information from your investigators that on that day in the broader area of Konjevic Polje, there could not have been several thousand refugees from Srebrenica. I'm saying this because I know that, but I think that you, too, must have information to show that on that day and in that area, there couldn't have been several thousand refugees from Srebrenica. A second point I wish to make is that I have often been in a position as a communications officer to have access to data collected through intelligence and electronic monitoring, and I think that that information was always highly suspect, that it was never reliable. And if I may make a slight digression: In the military sense, this was a breakthrough from the encirclement round the forces of the 28th Division rather than --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DB --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the fleeing of refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't want to go into great length about the developments; I want to ask you questions. And you will be permitted to answer additional questions by Mr. Petrusic, but I have a limited amount of time, and I intend to get through my examination today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Can I just ask a clarification? Witness DB, when you said that information collected through intelligence and electronic is apparently unreliable, isn't that one of the basic ways of collecting information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was one of the ways of collecting information, and the intelligence body radio electronic reconnaissance platoons are subordinated to them, but so are the reconnaissance and sabotage detachment that every corps had, which, by infiltrating enemy territory, collected information. Intelligence information was also collected from the enemy media, the press, television, and the radio, and from other elements infiltrated into enemy territory, and in various other ways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Proceed, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You seem to be worried about the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, I'm concerned that I have a large amount of examination to get through with this witness and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You are sure that you will finish today?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: At the present rate, I'm not sure, that's why I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good. Does that mean that you would like to have more time?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I may. I can give you a better assessment, Your Honours, as the day progresses, but I'm expecting to get done today, but if the answers are as long as this last answer, then I will not get through today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Because I have information that the witness cannot stay longer, if that's right, than today.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I don't have that information, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I heard it, but -- so if that's true, you have to bear that in mind and ask us for more time if you need it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much, Judge Riad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's turn to another issue, Witness DB, and that is the Bosnian Muslim intercept capabilities and their attempts to intercept your communications. If you could turn to Prosecutor's Exhibit 750.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And Mr. Usher, on the English, I'm going to be referring to page 43, and I have a marked copy. The witness can use my copy once again. Again, Your Honours, 750 is an analysis by the VRS, prepared by the army of Republika Srpska, describing its situation in 1992. And on page 43 I'd like to read from the second full paragraph, about midway in that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the report of the VRS says, and I quote: "A special problem is the large number of privately-owned means of communication in the brigades and the lower tactical units, the so-called Motorolas, which cannot be controlled, as well as the undisciplined radio communications of operating staff in intelligence centres and VRS signals units. So far we have registered nine enemy interception groups, exceptionally well-manned and equipped." Now, Witness DB, this is the analysis of your army in 1992. Let me turn -- and this highlights a number of problems. The first problem is that people who were using VRS means of communication were undisciplined; they didn't always abide by the appropriate security requirements. And the second problems it highlights is that the enemy interception groups could listen; they were well-manned and they were well-equipped. That's the assessment of your army in 1992, isn't it? That's the assessment of your army in 1992 in respect of the enemy intercept capabilities, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, and now, I was a senior army officer who graduated from high-level military schools, and for ethical reasons and professional reasons, I consider myself competent to comment on the information that you are now quoting. I consider myself competent to comment on this. Ever since the army exists, emphasis has been on its combat readiness and capabilities, so highlighting our weaknesses and underlining the advantages of the enemy, this is typical of all armies. No one in any army, among superior officers, will say, "We are the best now," "We are superior," "No one can hurt us." On the contrary; all shortcomings are underlined, whereas the advantages of the enemy are emphasised, and that is the logic applied in any army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let us turn to the next exhibit, which will be Prosecutor's Exhibit 825. And for this exhibit, Mr. President, I'm going to ask that it be under seal and that we go into private session to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Just -- I would like to ask Witness DB, without wasting time: What you said about highlighting the advantages of the enemy, are you just speaking of the equipment of interception or in general, as a general rule, you should always highlight that the enemy is better than you? Is that good for the morale of the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The enemy is never underestimated when working with troops, regarding all the elements of combat readiness, including the ability to intercept messages. For instance, on all our telephone extensions, we have a written message: "Take care. The enemy is listening." This was the rule 10 years ago and 20 years ago, and it still is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Are we in private session?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, we're not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Private session. Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in public session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness DB, it was possible for the enemy to intercept your telephone calls because, based on your information, the enemy had a very efficient system of interception; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of this analysis of combat readiness, it is stated there that the enemy did have an efficient system of interception.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were aware, weren't you, that the enemy was indeed focusing on your communications while you were engaged in the Srebrenica and the Zepa operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I assumed they were doing that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you dispute the fact that they did in fact capture communications that were being made by members of the VRS who participated in that operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then let us turn to the next exhibit, if we could, which would be Prosecutor's Exhibit 137. Take a look at that for just a moment, Witness DB.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you move the ELMO a little bit forward? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to look at Prosecutor's Exhibit 137, Witness DB?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If it could be placed on the ELMO, then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a list of VRS code names that were used during the time period of July and August of 1995. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me turn to the item that is the second from the end which is "Bedem." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Bedem the code name for the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm finished with this exhibit. Thank you very much, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday when you answered a question for my colleague Mr. Petrusic, you answered in the following fashion, and I'm going to read from the LiveNote page 7096, and I'm going to read lines 8 through 21. I will only read part of your answer. My colleague asked you the following question: "In the course of the proceedings so far, we have seen a great deal of markings, and I don't want to put them on the ELMO, but I'm going to give you an example. For example, Zlatar 1 as a name and 01. Can you explain to us what that means, Zlatar 1 and 01?" Now, you gave a long answer, and I'm only going to read part of it, and I will pick it up at line 15. "Then in going through the other code names and a review of them, it states that the rear command post is Zlatar 1, but the forward command post is Zlatar 2, and if we define a reserve post, if that is defined as well and stipulated, then that could be Zlatar 3." Now, I'm going to stop at this part of your answer and ask you, Zlatar 1, when you say the rear command post, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rear command post is a building or a room accommodating rear organs, that is logistic bodies, which are, as a rule, behind the command post, deep within our territory. There may also be some other corps bodies there, and it must always be ready, should the need arise to pull out our forces and move the basic command post, to take over the role of a command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "rear command post" -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that we need to clarify the translation. The witness said the rear command post is an area in the ground, if I understand the witness correctly. He didn't mean a building or anything, a piece of ground, which need not be a building or a premise, simply an area on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me put it in more concrete terms, Witness DB. Where was the rear command post for the Drina Corps in July and August of 1995, by your definition of rear command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In practice, as it was in the command of the Drina Corps, both the command post and the rear command post were right next to one another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the rear command post in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me read on in your answer, picking up at line 18 through 21. "In the rules and regulations that exist in the army, the mark 01 or 02 does not exist anywhere, although, in wartime practice, it is frequently used, that is to say, the commanding officers who were commanders or chiefs or suchlike." So as I understand your answer, as I understand your answer, "01" designated, in the wartime practice, the commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the person who is in command of that area, who is in command of that code name, and who introduces himself using that code name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if we could take a look at the next exhibit, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 635, Witness, this is an intercepted communication, and it is an interception, and I will read part of it, and I'd like you to comment on it. The participants are Zlatar and possibly Palma. "Z: Give me Palma ?: Sorry? Z: Palma. ?: Just a moment. Z: Is that Palma? P: Yes? Z: Give me 01." Now, 01 would be the commander according to the wartime practice that you've described; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then if we go down on this intercept further, we see a line that reads, "Tell him it's Zlatar 01 calling and ask what's new over there." Zlatar is the code name for which unit or brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zlatar was a secret name of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when we -- this intercept refers to Zlatar 01, this refers to the commander of the Drina Corps, in your opinion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's go further down this intercept, and we will see -- you can see the portion that says: "They're not able to reach the commander. Z: Yes. P: He said who should he call when he gets a chance? Z: Zlatar 385. P: Zlatar 385? Z: Yes and tell him to hurry up and call me." Now, Witness, this is a conversation with Zlatar 01 who later gives a phone number Zlatar 385. Are you familiar with the digits 385?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll explain briefly. In the preparation for testifying here, lawyer Petrusic asked me what this Zlatar 385 could mean. I answered that there were two possibilities. One of them was that this could be an extension of the three digit switchboard from Han Pijesak, or it could be a number, an identification number from one of the senior officers from the list of identification numbers, and that would be my answer to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So to clarify your answer, the second part, so this could be a telephone number of a senior officer at Zlatar, which is the command of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be an extension, a destination where an extension ends. All the extensions were from the automatic switchboard of Crna Rijeka, or Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. it could be an identification number denoting a senior officer and his position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, thank you very much. We'll now turn our attention to another area, which is the forward command posts generally in -- first of all, let me turn my attention to the forward command post in Krivace which existed, according to your testimony, from approximately the 12th of August until the 2nd -- I'm sorry, the 12th of July until the 2nd of August. Now, Witness DB, where did General Krstic spend his nights when he was at the forward command post in Krivace and later at the other two forward command posts that were set up for the Zepa operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would inform us that he was going to spend the night not far from that location, in the Kusace village, at the relatives of his wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why would he leave the forward command post to spend the night with his relatives?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: We understood that the time, because his health at the time was poor, at least two or three times during the day he would rebandage his leg, take off his prosthetic leg; he would walk with great difficulty, and we had only tents at this forward command post, and there was one demolished barn or something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the sanitary conditions, living in tents, was not sufficient to meet the medical needs of General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment really on his decision to spend the nights elsewhere, but we thought that was primarily for health and sanitary reasons and in view of the available accommodation facilities, because General Krstic spent most of his time on the front line together with his soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's turn our attention to the forward command post at Pribicevac, which was established on the 5th of July and, according to your testimony, was no longer in existence after the night of the 11th of July. During that period of time, did you ever -- did you stay at the forward command post? Did you spend your night in a tent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I slept in a tent or in a communications vehicle or in a dugout, one of the dugouts which were available there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many members of the communications group were with you at the forward command post in Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: About five or six.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did the communications centre operate on a 24-hour basis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it you had shifts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many persons were on a shift and what others were worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the day, everybody would work; and in nighttime, one person was on duty, taking care of all the devices, all the communications, because during the night we had no combat -- we had no ongoing combat operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "everybody would work," what does that mean? Did they work inside the van? Did they work outside the van?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The coder, the coding person, was always in the vehicle, because that's where the equipment was, and there was another soldier who monitored the work of all the others within the radio network.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: And those who were -- who had been on duty during the night would take the day off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So those two people you've described, they worked inside the van, I take it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since General Krstic was unable to get into the car with his prosthetic leg and his fresh wound, we would always take the radio equipment he used to issue orders out of the vehicle and near a tree or some place where he could sit down, and we would also enable him from the place where he was sitting to use the telephone and contact his superior command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what were your specific duties at that location? What specifically did you do during those few days that the forward command post communications centre existed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: My principal duty was to ensure quality and uninterrupted communication on all lines, and I also did some other jobs which General Krstic would order me to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Such as? What other jobs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: For instance, since there were few of us officers at the forward command post, he would order me to inspect the guards at night, to ensure alertness and see to it that the guards are awake, to check on them briefly. I told you yesterday that he had ordered me to admit UNPROFOR representatives. Sometimes also I would convey one of his messages, but normally, I would concentrate on providing quality and uninterrupted communication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you ever leave the forward command post communications centre other than the episode you described in respect of the United Nations soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not from Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the 7th and 8th of July, did you hear every radio communication that was made from the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that with certainty. If I was right there by the equipment, I would certainly hear it; otherwise there would be one of my soldiers there always who were trained to monitor the quality of communication and see to it that there are no interruptions among any of the participants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear every radio communication between the 8th of July until the time the communications centre was dismantled, was packed up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think not. I would always concentrate on my job with the equipment when the combat operations were intensive and when there was something important going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the equipment broke down -- we heard, for example, the teleprinters, according to General Krstic, frequently broke down. Whose job was it to take care of the teleprinters, to fix the equipment, maintain the equipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you yesterday that those breakdowns in communications were not frequent and that I did not agree with that. And I told you always that we carried with us a back-up teleprinter, teletype. There was always the possibility, if a teleprinter would break down, which happened, we could ask by telephone to borrow a teleprinter from the logistics organs and have it taken --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't mean to interrupt you. I need to -- if you would just answer my question, which was: Who was it who repaired the equipment when there was a mechanical breakdown?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The equipment was repaired by mechanics, people who were trained to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you participate in the repairs or were you not trained to do so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some simple things which did not exceed normal maintenance, I could manage.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Judge Riad, you informed me that between an hour and 70 minutes would be an appropriate time. I'm about to move to a different subject, so we've been going for one hour. This would be an appropriate moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So would be more logical to stop now?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And would you able to know if you need more time today?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I will know by the next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So that I can inform the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you. Anyhow, we are ready, if the information I had is confirmed that the witness cannot stay after today.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Judge Riad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So we'll have a break of 20 minutes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Riad. If the witness -- if the usher could be given Prosecutor's Exhibits 764/1 through 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, do you have an answer concerning your --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: At the conclusion of this session I should be in a better position to know, not at the beginning. I shall find out as I progress.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Usher, I'm going to call out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So everybody should be ready to continue after 3.00. That seems to be a precaution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But not for too long.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you. These exhibits, Your Honours, Prosecutor's Exhibit 764/1 through 764/20, were documents that were seized at the Bratunac Brigade pursuant to a search warrant that was issued by the Tribunal. Mr. Usher, if you could place 764/1A on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Witness, this document, as you can see, is a bill, and it is a bill from the Hotel Fontana to the command of the Bratunac Brigade, and as you can see, it is accommodation for your representatives in the Hotel Fontana in July. The total bill on this was 6.341 dinars. Now, let me turn to the next exhibit, and I'll have you comment on the next exhibit, which is 764/20A.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If that could be placed on the ELMO and the B/C/S given to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, this is also a bill, part of a bill for 1.980 dinars, and it lists the people who stayed at the hotel. And can you tell me, do you -- can you identify the name Goran Stakic? Do you know that name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about the next name, Boro Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Novica Pajic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that during that time, he was chief the staff of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next name, Vukota Vukovic, I believe we identified him yesterday; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Vidoje -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Vidoje Blagojevic, he was the commander of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the name Colonel Popovic, who is Colonel Popovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew a Lieutenant Colonel Popovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What position did he have in the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the period for which this bill was issued, he was chief of security of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could turn -- and it appears on the invoice that Colonel Popovic stayed for six nights at the hotel, as did Blagojevic; and Vukovic stayed for a total of 17 nights. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn to Prosecutor's Exhibit 764/8A. This is another bill dated the 15th of July, 1995, and this is accommodation for Colonel Vujadin Popovic for two nights. Now, is this the same Vujadin Popovic you knew to be the commander of security, assistant commander for security?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could turn to Prosecutor's Exhibit 764/9A.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a remark to make regarding Mr. Harmon's question. Mr. Harmon said that this was accommodation for Colonel Popovic for two nights on the exhibit, on this exhibit as well as the previous ones; however, in the Serbo-Croat document that we have in our possession, no mention is made of the number of nights but only the sum. I wouldn't go into what that means, but in any event, the number of overnights is not mentioned in any of these documents that Mr. Harmon has been reviewing. So I'm not sure what the witness is asked to confirm, the correctness of the invoice or the number of overnight stays. Perhaps we should be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'll be glad to be more precise, Judge Riad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Thank you, Mr. Visnjic. Proceed, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we turn, Mr. Usher, to Prosecutor's Exhibit 764/10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this also is an invoice. It's dated the 15th of July, 1995. Can you identify the individual in this, Lieutenant Colonel Krsmanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What position did he hold in the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that, at the time, he was chief of the transportation service in the logistics body.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And for the benefit of the Chamber, Lieutenant Colonel Krsmanovic appears on the organogram in this position. Let's turn to Prosecutor's Exhibit 764/11. This is an invoice dated the 15th of July and it identifies a Colonel Cerovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a Colonel Cerovic and what position he held in the Drina Corps command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the assistant for morale, religious, and legal affairs in the command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And Your Honours, Colonel Cerovic appears in the organogram in this position. Could we turn to Prosecutor's Exhibit 764/9A, which is another invoice for the 15th of July, indicating the number 11 under "amount."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is Lieutenant Colonel Lazar Acanovic? Do you know that name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: He worked in the rear services of the Drina Corps. There were some replacements, but I think at this time he was assistant for logistics of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again referring to the organogram, Your Honours, Colonel Acanovic appears in this position. Let us turn to Prosecutor's Exhibit 764/6. This is a bill dated the 14th of July. It says in the body of the text: "Accommodation in the Hotel Fontana in a three-bed room, 207, on 10, 11 and 12 July," and the amount is 3, and it identifies three individuals: Lieutenant Colonel Milovan Milutinovic. Do you know that individual and what position he held in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know him personally, but I think he could have been a senior officer working in the information service in the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska. I know him by name and not personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second individual listed is Lieutenant Colonel Slobodan Stancevic. Do you know that individual?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let's turn to the next exhibit, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 764/7A. This is accommodation in the Hotel Fontana in two identified rooms on 10, 11, and 12 July. And again, to shed light on Mr. Visnjic's concern, the amount listed may well correspond to the number of days that are indicated in the text accompanying this bill. There are some individuals identified: Milutin Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that individual? Have you heard of that individual?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zoran Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zoran Kulic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us turn to Prosecutor's Exhibit 764/15A. This is a bill that identifies individuals. It's dated the 23rd of July, 1995. Do you know a Nebojsa Subotic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A Slobodan Perovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A D. Bogojevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the other two individuals on this bill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn to Prosecutor's Exhibit 764/18. This is a bill dated the 27th of July. It lists six individuals. Do you know any of those named individuals? Can you identify them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn to the next exhibit, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 764/19A, a bill dated the 28th of July, 1995. It identifies five individuals. Can you identify any of those five individuals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us turn to Prosecutor's Exhibit 764/2. This is a bill dated the 6th of July, 1995. And the text reads: "Accommodation in Hotel Fontana Bratunac for General Radislav Krstic, room 204, and general's Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. escorts, Vlado Tosic and Dalibor Krstic, in room 10, on 5/6 July 1995." The two individuals with General Krstic, Vlado Tosic and Dalibor Krstic, do you know those individuals and what position they held?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know them. They were drivers and also the closest escorts of General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn to the last exhibit in this particular series, Prosecutor's Exhibit 764/3A, a bill dated the 14th of July, 1995. This identifies accommodations in the Hotel Fontana from 5 to 13 July 1995 for General Krstic, Vladimir Tosic, who you've identified as one of his drivers. Let me turn my attention to the remaining names. Colonel Obrad Vicic, who appears to have stayed in the amount of 1. Who is Colonel Obrad Vicic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Obrad Vicic, at the time, was one of the operations officers in the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his relationship in respect of General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean in the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: De facto, what was his relationship with General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was at Pribicevac, at the forward command post both at Pribicevac and Zepa. He was the operations officer there, and also Krstic's deputy at the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At both forward command posts, the one in Srebrenica [sic] and the one in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is Colonel Obrad Vicic today, do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Belgrade. He has retired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us turn to Lieutenant Colonel Svetozar Kosoric, who we have identified previously as the chief of intelligence in the intelligence section of the Drina Corps. He appears to have stayed eight units. And the last individual is Dalibor Krstic, who you've identified as the driver of General Krstic. Now, Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And Mr. Usher, I've completed with this series of exhibits.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that General Krstic had a new prosthesis and he needed, it was your opinion, sanitary accommodations to take care of his medical situation. General Krstic spent the nights away from the forward command post in Pribicevac, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he spent those nights at the Hotel Bratunac, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the bills, he would just tell us if anything urgent should arise, that we should reach him through the command of the Bratunac Brigade, because he said that in the evening he would go to the command of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To pick up his messages or to check on messages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If anything urgent should happen, that we could reach him through the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, so I thought he was going there to spend the night in one of their premises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let us turn, then, to -- let me ask you another question, Witness DB. You have mentioned on occasion that you provided a signalsman for General Krstic. When General Krstic would leave the forward command post at night from Pribicevac, and he would go to Bratunac, did he have with him a signalsman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Excuse me, I just have one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I think it -- do you -- it's more for you, maybe, to clarify one of your questions, than it is for the witness, but let me ask it anyway and we can decide. On these nights on your question you've mentioned on occasion -- well, "He spent those nights at the Hotel Bratunac, didn't he?" That's your question. I don't know which nights. I'm sorry, the screen has gone away, and I just want to clarify which dates we're talking about. I think it's either you can ask the question or --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I can ask the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The operation in Pribicevac, the forward command post existed from the 5th to, according to your testimony, the night of the 11th, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And each of those nights, General Krstic did not spend the night at the forward command post, he spent the night in Bratunac; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Does that clarify the matter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Yes, it does, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's stay focused on the forward command post at Pribicevac, and when was the first time that you saw General Zivanovic at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think two or three days prior to the 11th. Sometime around the 9th of July or on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the day when he arrived at the forward command post with General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to my recollection, he was always with General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had an opportunity to be an observer at the forward command post. Did it appear to you that General Zivanovic had an important role in commanding the operation against Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my recollection, he didn't interfere significantly with the command of the operation, but that the operation initially up to the 9th was under the command of General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So up to the 9th, General Zivanovic was not -- did not play an important role in directing and commanding the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he didn't. That is my impression that I had as a communications man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the arrival of General Mladic at the forward command post was not something that was unusual, based on your experience in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, frequently, I believe your testimony was, General Mladic, because he was the commander of the army, would appear at the forward command posts in significant offensive operations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When General Mladic appeared at the forward command post with General Zivanovic, did he consult with General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In any event, they did talk about something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a participant in those conversations, or did you merely observe from afar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not participate in those conversations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it appear to you that there was a disagreement on the operation itself when General Mladic arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some particular disagreement I did not notice, but I just know that, once General Mladic arrived, he stayed very briefly at the forward command post; and then with General Krstic and General Zivanovic, he went to the observation post, which was about 500 metres away from the forward command post, from which the whole area of Srebrenica can be seen; and from then on, I could follow events only over the radio waves, so I couldn't follow personally or visually. I couldn't observe things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to the best of your recollection, this was the 9th of July, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that General Mladic arrived for the first time to the forward command post about two days prior to the military fall of Srebrenica, so I have roughly judged that it could be the 9th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when -- let me withdraw that. General Mladic was the chief of the army, and it was within his prerogative as chief of the army to make changes in the strategic plan to capture the enclave of Srebrenica, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is his right as the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you testified that during the past -- during your past experiences with General Mladic, it is customary for him to get on the radio and exhort his troops, congratulate his troops, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there was success, he would congratulate them and urge them on in the implementation of their combat assignments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when there was success, it was not uncommon for General Mladic to issue additional orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not unusual.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nor was it unusual for him to urge his troops to move on, to advance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you have testified earlier that you did not hear every -- you were not present around the command communications centre to hear every communication that was being issued between the 8th and the 11th of July, if I recall your testimony accurately.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but immediately after saying that, I also added that I would focus my attention on the equipment at times when combat activities were highly dynamic and intensive. As far as I remember, that is what I said, and that was quite logical.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when -- and you heard in this situation, you have reported to this Trial Chamber, that General Mladic urged the troops on into Srebrenica, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: He urged them to continue with the attack after having reached the positions they had reached.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at one point I think you told us that he urged General -- I'm sorry, Colonel or Lieutenant Colonel Vinko Pandurevic to proceed up a particular axis, avoiding a potential point of resistance, a mountain of some kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic, but I said that he urged Colonel Andric, with his unit, to go round that feature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I stand corrected, thank you. When General Mladic gave the order that you have reported to Colonel Andric, was he in your presence or was he away from you? Did you hear this order over the radio?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it over the radio, the radio equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was General Krstic with General Mladic at the time he gave -- Mladic gave the order to Colonel Andric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know and can you tell the Judges what degree of consultation between General Mladic and General Krstic preceded the order that you heard on the radio, urging Colonel Andric to proceed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there were any consultations, then they were between them on the spot, wherever they happened to be. So I cannot tell what kind of consultations they had, if any; I'm just telling you what I heard over the radio transmitters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when General Mladic gave the order to some of the units to proceed toward Srebrenica, was General Zivanovic still the commander of the Drina Corps, and was General Krstic still the Chief of Staff of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when there is a strategic change by the chief of the army, in other words, in this case move from position "A" to position "B," whose role is it to ensure that the orders issued by General Mladic were implemented?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: If General Mladic issues an order in person to the Corps Commander or to the Chief of Staff of the corps, then the latter is the one to implement those orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if General Mladic issues an order to a brigade commander, let's take Colonel Andric, for example, is it the -- does General Zivanovic and General Krstic have to ensure that General Mladic's order is implemented?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The orders given by General Mladic in those days were carried out directly. I heard when Colonel Andric simply said, "Yes, sir" and proceeded forward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you, did you, from your position, hear at any time General Krstic disagree with the orders that were given by General Mladic to advance into Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not hear that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When General Mladic issued the orders to proceed into Srebrenica, did the chain of command within the Drina Corps remain intact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that commanders executed orders given them then by General Mladic, without objection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the chain of command, the normal chain of command in the Drina Corps structure, was not ruptured by virtue of General Mladic giving an order to Colonel Andric to advance into Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I had been in Mladic's shoes, I would have given -- I would have conveyed that order to the commander of the corps or the person in control of the operation. I don't understand the question, because the chain of command can never be broken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, the chain of command remained intact throughout the Srebrenica operation, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you -- let me change the subject. We're going to switch gears, Witness DB, and we're going to focus our attention at this point on the 10th Sabotage Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And if the witness could be shown Prosecutor's Exhibit 158, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the individuals -- first of all, do you recognise General Krstic in that picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recognise the individuals with the numbers 1, 2, and 3 on them? Not personally, but do you recognise the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say. I don't know -- recognise these insignia and I don't recognise anyone in person. I know approximately the insignia of the 10th Sabotage Unit, but I don't seem to recognise any of these people in the picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, this isn't the clearest of pictures, but these individuals, numbers 1, 2, and 3, have been identified by a previous witness, Drazen Erdemovic, as being his colleagues within the 10th Sabotage Detachment. And do you know who the commander of the 10th Sabotage Detachment was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that period, it was Lieutenant Miso Pelemis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see Lieutenant Miso Pelemis when you were at the forward command post or a participant in the Srebrenica operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I knew that his unit was located there and that they had arrived much later than we did, around the 9th or the 10th perhaps, but I saw his signalsman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's talk about that. When do you recall seeing his -- the 10th Sabotage Detachment's signalsman? Approximately what day?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, I'm done with this exhibit. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it was two or three days after the commencement of combat operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So -- okay. Now, where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him in the area of Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of Pribicevac, not exactly on the location of the forward command post, but in that village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And was he accompanied by anybody, this signalsman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I only know that we discussed communications, and I asked him whether his unit was there and he said yes. Then I asked him about the communications system, since they were not in our plan, whether he had any information would they need communication lines with the forward command post. He said he didn't know. He said they had Motorolas and they had internal communications. That was the unit which reluctantly carried those devices which we had, because they were too heavy for them, and they carried only Motorolas for the most part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say "in the village of Pribicevac," I'm trying to get you to recall, if you can, the distance from the forward command post where you had communication with this signalsman. Was it within ten metres, a hundred metres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, about 100 metres. He was going toward the observation post because he was a signalsman, and since Srebrenica is in a deep valley, I concluded then that his unit had some special axis [Realtime transcript read in error "access"] through a canyon, and he had to remain on the top there in order to cover the movements of his unit with his communications. So he was passing by the forward command post towards that elevation, and that's when I stopped him and asked him about the communications.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the time you stopped him, was General Krstic at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was either at the forward command post or at the observation post, which was about 400 or 500 metres away from the forward command post. He was in one of those places for sure, because I saw him in the middle of the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the observation post where the signalsman from the 10th Sabotage Battalion or Detachment was going was the observation post where General Krstic was located; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is close by that feature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General Krstic was aware that the 10th Sabotage Detachment had arrived on either the 9th or the 10th of July, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he knew that this unit had arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you a little something about the communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, excuse me, if I may say very briefly. In line 13, it was interpreted that the unit had a special access through the canyon, and the witness said that the unit had a special direction, which is "axis" in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Can we verify that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The transcript -- the English transcript, Witness DB, says, "I concluded then that the unit had some special access through a canyon." Can you clarify what you meant when you said that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their route, the direction of their movement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, let's talk about the communications that was available to the 10th Sabotage Detachment. I believe you said they were Motorolas. Those are hand-held devices, are they not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: They usually used that kind of equipment, those devices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you're a military man, Witness DB. There was active combat going on, offensive operations in Srebrenica. The 10th Sabotage Detachment appeared. They appeared to be attacking in a certain direction toward Srebrenica. There were other Drina Corps units, such as the Drina Wolves, also advancing in the same direction; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Two units cannot use the same direction to attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You misunderstood me. Perhaps I wasn't clear. The objective was in the same general direction, and when one conducts offensive operations, there's usually a unit to your right and a unit to your left; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from a military point of view, it is absolutely imperative that the unit on the right know about the unit on the left and the position of each unit; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the reason that's true is because units from the same side, if they are not in communication, may well find themselves casualties because the -- one of the units may fire upon the unit, thinking it is the enemy; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. That happens sometimes too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when the 10th Sabotage Detachment was advancing along a particular axis, is it your opinion that the 10th Sabotage Detachment had to coordinate with the units on its right and the units on its left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. That is why I discussed with their signalsman the arrangements and we tried to resolve that problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we've seen earlier in documents that I've presented to you that Motorolas are interceptable communications. By that, I mean they are capable of being intercepted by the enemy.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. That's why I didn't use them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've also said that General Krstic, General Mladic were together during this time period that the offensive operation -- well, let me rephrase that question -- that General Mladic and General Krstic were together during the offensive operations. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were together in the period when General Mladic was at the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General Krstic and General Mladic had Motorolas with them during the period of this operation, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about General Mladic because I was not at the observation post, but I think that General Krstic could not have had a Motorola under any circumstances because we had protected communications with all the units that were under his command, and I think it would have been quite illogical for him to use a Motorola. I don't know who he could have communicated with through a Motorola.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you ever tell an investigator from the office of the Prosecutor that General Mladic and General Krstic had Motorolas and communicated with them during the Srebrenica operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were together, the two of them were together. If you mean the communication between them, or you mean their communication with the units?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, my question is this: Did you ever tell an investigator, Jean-Rene Ruez, that General Mladic and General Krstic had Motorolas and communicated with them during the Srebrenica operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that I have said that about General Mladic, for instance, because he talked over these devices without any concern about interception.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we have Prosecutor's Exhibit 818 shown to the witness, please. If you would just show it to the witness first so he can examine it, and then we'll put it onto ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Witness, I'd like to direct your attention to General Krstic, and particularly his left hand. Now, this is not a particularly good-quality photograph, it's taken from a video, but what does it appear is in the left hand of General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be sure, Mr. Prosecutor. You probably assume it's a Motorola, in view of your preceding questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that appear to be an antenna sticking out ahead of General Krstic's hand? Let me try to assist you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I really can't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me try to assist you a little further with this. We're going to play a film of this particular section, and it's going to be played in slow motion, and I'd like you -- and I'll play it more than once, but I'd like you to pay attention to General Krstic and what is in his hand. So if we could have Prosecutor's Exhibit 145/2 played, and we may replay this more than once. This is a film taken on the 11th of July, Witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Colonel Trivic is on the right. He has a Motorola in his hand, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You need to see that film again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I must admit that the film is much clearer than the photograph, and at one point -- we can repeat it, perhaps -- he was really holding something in his hand, and it looks like an antenna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does a Motorola hand-held communication device have an antenna similar to the one you saw in this film?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Antennas vary in length, but there is one which can be three or four, up to 20 centimetres long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let me ask you finally, in your opinion, is General Krstic carrying a Motorola in the film that you just saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say with certainty. I cannot confirm with certainty, but he's holding something in his hand which looks like an antenna. I cannot see the device, but there is something like an antenna since that's what we're discussing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it assist you to see the film again, or would it not assist you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've followed the hand. The device is as big as a fist, approximately, so I can't see the device, but I can clearly see something like an antenna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, we will not pursue that topic any further. Thank you very much. Actually, I will ask you one additional question. Witness, these hand-held devices, if that is a Motorola device, and if the 10th Sabotage Detachment had Motorolas, and if General Mladic had a Motorola, were both Generals Mladic and Krstic capable of communicating with the 10th Sabotage Detachment via Motorola?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: If everybody had the same device, the same equipment, and they were all following the same plan and the same frequencies, then they could hear each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm about to go into a different subject, and I have, frankly, lost track of the time. I don't know how much time is remaining to me in this segment, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: How much time do you need for this segment?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Probably 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Can we have a break now, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good, then you will have more time. We'll have a break of 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Riad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DB, I'd like to focus your attention now on the 11th of July, which is the day when Srebrenica was entered, the town of Srebrenica was entered by the VRS soldiers. I'm going to summarise your testimony of that day, and you can tell me if I have correctly understood your testimony. But in reading your testimony, your testimony said that Generals Mladic, Krstic, and Zivanovic went into Srebrenica on the 11th of July at 1700 or 1800 hours, that they never returned to the forward command post, that you remained at the forward command post until approximately 1900 hours, when you packed up your communications centre and departed for Bratunac through Potocari and, when you left, there was no other form of communications remaining at the forward command post. Did I fairly summarise your testimony of yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They didn't come back to the forward command post while I was there. You said they never went back after that, but I think I said that no one came to the forward command post while I was there, which means until about 1900 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And other than that, I fairly summarised your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified that you packed up the communications vehicle, and I'm interested in the term "packed up." Does that mean that you disassembled the communications facilities in and around the forward command post, put them in your communications vehicle, and essentially departed Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the elements of the communications centre that I had installed on behalf of the Drina Corps I packed up and left Pribicevac. Only minor elements could remain at the forward command post, wire connections of the Bratunac Brigade and the battalion that was there, but I think that they too, with the troops, had gone forward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you packed up the communications vehicle and you went down to Bratunac and then later that evening went to Vlasenica, was the communications vehicle functional? Could it communicate by, for example, teleprinter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what period?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the time of approximately 1900 hours on the 11th, when you left Pribicevac, to the time you arrived in Vlasenica that evening, around midnight.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was not possible to communicate via teleprinter. The closest teleprinter there was was in the command of the Bratunac Brigade, in their communications centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you continue to communicate via radio from the communications vehicle during the same period of time I've just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: A soldier with a mobile radio transmitter stayed on in Bratunac on the 11th to the 12th, and he was at General Krstic's disposal and he was able to use that communication to communicate with the directly subordinated units participating in the operation Krivaja 95.
