He could use elements and communications of the communications centre in the Bratunac Brigade headquarters when he was there, but the communications I had packed up could not be used by him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... did not in fact communicate with anybody; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he communicated with anybody. I told you --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You misunderstood what I was saying. The communications vehicle that you had did not engage in any form of communications from the time you left Pribicevac through the period of time when you arrived at Vlasenica headquarters around midnight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no communication from that vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me turn to the testimony of General Krstic and read this to you. And for the benefit of counsel and Your Honours, I'm referring to the English language version 19 October 2000, page 6198, lines 6 through 23. And to put this in context for you, Witness DB, General Krstic is testifying about the events on the 11th of July and after he has conducted his walk through town with General Mladic and General Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my colleague Mr. McCloskey asked General Krstic the following questions: "So you left Srebrenica and went to Bratunac?" Krstic: "No, I didn't leave Srebrenica for Bratunac. Immediately after we had received the order and had been informed about the meeting, the time of the meeting and my presence there, I went back to the Pribicevac forward command post along the Srebrenica-Bojna-Zeleni Jadar-Pribicevac axis, so I went back." "Q. Who did you find at Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the Pribicevac forward command post, I found Colonel Vicic, Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric, and the commander of the staff command, Lieutenant Amovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So those were probably already evening hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was already evening, around eight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at that point leave Pribicevac and go to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I had briefed Colonel Vicic about what General Mladic had ordered, that is, that the units should stop at the lines and stabilise their positions, I ordered Colonel Vicic to continue monitoring the situation in the units. After that, I left for Bratunac along the Pribicevac-Sase-Bratunac route." That concludes this portion of the transcript. Now, the units that General Krstic asked Colonel Vicic to monitor were the units that were participating in the offensive operations against Srebrenica, and my question to you, Witness DB, is, how could Colonel Vicic monitor the situation of the units that were engaged in the offensive operations if he had no communications at Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: So all three of them, General Krstic, Vicic, and Kosoric, after I had left, returned to Pribicevac. That is what General Krstic said in his statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me -- what is correct is that when General Krstic returned, he identified Colonel Vicic, Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric, and Lieutenant Amovic as being present.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: A soldier with a mobile device always accompanied General Krstic. If what General Krstic said is correct, then it is quite possible that they used that device, that Colonel Vicic used that device that accompanied General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is this, however: How could Colonel Vicic monitor the situation in the units if he did not have communications available to him at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is correct that he monitored the situation in the unit, he might perhaps have used the device that was with General Krstic, or the device of the Bratunac Brigade forward command post if Colonel Blagojevic returned to Pribicevac with that device. Those were the only possibilities. There were no others, technically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your answer is that it is possible that Colonel Vicic could have communicated with General Krstic in Bratunac from the Pribicevac forward command post on the night of the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he couldn't. If he used a radio communication with units from Pribicevac, but he could not communicate with anyone in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you suppose General -- I mean, if the situation developed that there was a major problem with the units that were operating in Srebrenica -- let me give you a hypothetical. Let's assume the 28th Division reappeared and started offensive operations -- or counter-offensive operations against the units that were VRS units. How was Colonel Vicic, who was supposed to be monitoring the situation of those units, supposed to convey a message to the command that was in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Technically, it was not possible. It was not possible to communicate a message from Pribicevac to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is it possible that -- is it possible, Witness DB, that you could be confused as to when you left the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that I left about 1900 hours, maybe 1930, on the 11th, because, judging by my movement when I passed through Potocari, darkness had just fallen; and when I reached Bratunac, it was already quite dark, and I'm absolutely sure of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible, Witness DB, that you could be confused on the date when you left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We discussed that with the investigators, because after I arrived at Bratunac, I was present immediately at the first meeting, held at 2200 hours in the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, so it is not possible under any circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me turn my attention now to Defence Exhibit 80, and if the witness could be given Defence Exhibit 80. If you could place Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the English version on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I read it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember ever having seen this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me first of all read this -- what General Krstic had to say about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And Your Honours, that is on the English language version of the transcript of the 19th of October. I'm starting on page 6199 and I will read over to the following page, 6200, line 14.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My colleague, Mr. Petrusic, was examining General Krstic at the time, and he asked, "Could we have Exhibit 80, please." Question by

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: "So you reached the forward command post at Pribicevac from Srebrenica, you issued certain assignments to Colonel Vicic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exhibit 80 bears the number 03/4-1617, dated the 11th of July, 1995. It is issued by the Main Staff of the army of the Republika Srpska by assistant commander Major General Milan Gvero to the Drina Corps command at the forward command post number 1. Were you familiar with the contents of this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I went back to the forward command post at Pribicevac from Srebrenica, I was given this document and was familiar with its content. It is directly addressed to the Drina Corps of the forward command post number 1 of the Drina Corps at Pribicevac. Just as I was familiar with the previous warning with respect to UNPROFOR, so I also studied the document sent by the assistant commander for morale, legal, and religious issues, General Gvero." And that ends his answer. Now, I'd like you to focus your attention on the exhibit itself, and one can see that this exhibit, in the upper left-hand corner, has been issued by the Main Staff on the 11th of July, and there are two addressees, one of which is the Drina Corps forward command post number 1, and it is signed by assistant commander Major General Milan Gvero. Now, you have in front of you -- my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, before the question is put to the witness, for the benefit of the witness, the interpreter said -- misinterpreted something as if General Krstic had sat with General Gvero, but in fact he had read it afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's correct. He did not sit with General Gvero, and we would so stipulate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us take a look at the document that General Krstic says he received at the forward command post on the night of the 11th. First of all, the form of the document. Can you tell me, is this a document that was sent by teleprinter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This has been processed by teleprinter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the -- referring to the B/C/S version, Defence Exhibit 80B, do you see some handwriting in the lower right-hand corner of this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is a notation as to the date and the time when this document was received; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is a document that General Krstic says he received at the forward command post. There appears to be a signature next to that document. Can you identify that signature, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have been trying to do that from the very beginning in order to see whether this document was received at the forward command post -- I'm thinking of the encoder or somewhere else -- but I assume that this document was received at the forward command post, because it doesn't have the stamp when the coder enters the information which is now inscribed in the lower right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So normally the -- at the Drina Corps headquarters, for example, the Drina Corps command, there's actually a stamp that has "received" and "processed," and it shows the date and the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the forward command post, was this the traditional way that you would note when telecommunications were received, in this form?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that we didn't have a sufficient number of stamps, so I assume that this was a document that was received outside the command of the Drina Corps, so I assume it was received at the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's turn to the next document, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 830. And if the witness could be shown Prosecutor's Exhibit 830, please. Now, you have the B/C/S version, and if the first page of the English version could be placed on the ELMO, Mr. Usher. Take a moment to examine that document, Witness DB. The substance isn't terribly important. I'm going to be asking you about certain features on this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, this is a document that is dated the 11th of July, 1995. It was issued -- on the B/C/S version you can see it. It was issued for the commander, Major General Zivanovic. And we will come to that detail in a minute. This order was issued to a number of commands, including the forward command post. Can you, by looking at this document, and particularly page 2 of this document, if we could have that on the ELMO, there appears to be a stamp at the bottom of this document. This is a document that was not received at the forward command post. Can you tell me, to the best of your ability, where this document was received?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was drafted in the Drina Corps command. It was typed out over there on a typewriter and carried to the communications centre, processed probably on a teleprinter, in terms of encoding, and at 2250 hours, the operator or encoder gave the telegram or message to the teleprinter station in the command of the Drina Corps to dispatch it to the listed commands. And then this document, such as we see it, a copy of it, was sent back to the mailing department of the Drina Corps command and, as such, it was archived, and we have a copy here before us. I don't know if I have been clear. Have you been able to follow?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The "received" stamp. This document was sent at some -- to various locations, and it was received on the 11th of July at 2230 hours, according to the stamp.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I would like to make myself quite clear, because this is my speciality. When the encryptor or encoder in the Drina Corps received this to encrypt it and send it to all the units, he signed that he received this document just as it now stands, at 2230 hours. Then he encrypted it, and to do that he needed 20 minutes. And at 2250 -- it is illegible, the word "processed" here. At 2250, he handed it over to the teleprinter station, to the Drina Corps command, so that they could forward it on by teleprinter to all the commands listed here at the beginning of the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was sent out from the Drina Corps command at 2250 hours to the various addressees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means immediately after 2250, without any delay, it was sent to all the units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you two minor details about this document. When this document was received by the addressees, it did not bear a signature because you could not send a signed document over the teleprinter, could you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Second question -- and I point this out for Your Honours. On the B/C/S version -- and Witness, you can help us with this -- there appears next to the word "commandant" the word "za." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does "za" mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this time, when all this was being created, it is quite certain that both General Zivanovic and General Krstic were attending the meeting in Bratunac. And then probably an order arrived from the Main Staff to the command of the Drina Corps in Vlasenica, and then the operations officer in the Drina Corps -- he may have been on duty, Colonel Predrag Jocic, because I see his signature here, so I assume it is his signature -- in the absence of both the commander and the Chief of Staff at headquarters, he wrote it out, this same order from the Main Staff, and had it sent to all units. I assume that is what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the word "za" signifies that Predrag Jocic signed on behalf of the commander, General Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And I note for the record, Your Honour, in the English translation of this exhibit, Prosecutor's Exhibit 840 [sic], there is no "for" in the signature block area. If one reads the English translation, one would assume that Major General Zivanovic himself signed this, so this document needs to be corrected for the record. Now we will turn to our last exhibit in this series, Witness DB. If I could have Prosecutor's Exhibit 831.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Harmon. In your previous statement, page 56, 10, you said "Exhibit 840."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I meant Exhibit 830, and the record should be corrected. Thank you. If you would give the witness the B/C/S version. Just a moment, please. Have Your Honours received Prosecutor's Exhibit 831?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: We have 833.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We need 831 distributed, so ... Take a moment to examine that document if you would, Witness DB, while it's being distributed to the parties. Mr. Usher, I need the English version of this placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, this is a document that in -- was issued by the Drina Corps command on the 11th of July. And this is a document that is identical, apparently, in substance to the previous document, and it was addressed to, among other locations, the IKM DK, which was the Drina Corps forward command post. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we could turn to the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And Mr. Usher, if you would place my copy of the B/C/S version on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, this is a document that was also received at the forward command post, was it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Comparing it with the previous document which was sent by General Gvero, it is obvious that the same encoding officer, encoder, received both documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, my question is in respect of Prosecutor's 831, the signature block, the handwritten "received" block, is identical, is it not, to the same document that I showed you two exhibits ago that General Krstic says he received at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The signature, it's the signature of the same encoder or operator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And not only is the signature identical to the exhibit that was received by General Krstic at the forward command post, but the print and the script and the numbers are identical, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Prosecutor's Exhibit 831 -- what time was this received at the forward command post at Pribicevac, according to the notation made on the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here at 2350 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, do you still maintain that the communications centre of the forward command post left at about 1900 hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I maintain is that all components of the communications centre which I had installed for the commanding of the Srebrenica operation -- now, I mean the encoding officer and all the components of the communication centre -- left with me around 1900 hours. And I'm now busy thinking and trying to get all the pieces to fit together in view of this possibility, of this situation. I cannot decipher the signature of the encoding operator and understand where this document could have been received.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, one possibility is that you have simply mistaken the date when you dismantled the forward command post. Is that a possibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is absolutely not possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, it is the Prosecution's submission that the communication centre at the forward command post did indeed remain on the night of the 11th and the morning of the 12th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us turn to another issue -- thank you very much for examining those documents, Witness DB. Let me turn to another aspect of your testimony, and that is your trip through Potocari on the evening of the 11th. And that trip took you through Potocari around dusk, you left around 1900 hours, and in your testimony you said that you saw elements of the Drina Corps mingled with refugees and with UN soldiers in and around the UN compound at Potocari. Now, this Trial Chamber has heard the testimonies of numerous UN soldiers and officers who were present in Potocari on the 10th, 11th, 12th, and ensuing days, and the testimony of those UN soldiers and officers is uniform in the point that there were no Bosnian Serb elements in and around the refugees and around them until the morning of the 12th of July, 1995. In addition to that, Witness, the Trial Chamber has heard the testimonies of numerous Bosnian Muslims who were in and around Potocari, and it was their testimonies, again uniformly on this point, that the Bosnian Serb soldiers did not appear in and around the compound until the 12th. Now, Witness, again let me ask you a question I've asked you before. Do you still maintain that you went down through Potocari on the 11th of July? And you can answer me that "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's talk about the elements of the VRS that you saw in and around Potocari. You've testified that they included elements of perhaps the Bratunac Brigade because you saw them conversing with the Muslim population. You also saw elements of the Drina Wolves, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked similar questions on several occasions by the investigator in April, and I told him the same thing as I will tell you now. Indeed, among this enormous crowd of civilians, I noticed a small number of soldiers of the army of Republika Srpska. I don't know whether those were small groups of the 10th Sabotage Detachment of the Drina Wolves or the Bratunac Brigade, but that was a small group of our soldiers and, in my testimony, I said that they looked to me as a small number of people curious to know what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DB --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- I'm sorry to interrupt you. Again, I have my eye on the clock, and you don't have to repeat your testimony; it's in the record. My question to you was, amongst the soldiers that you saw mingled with the population on the 11th of July, did you see members of the Drina Wolves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be certain whether it was them, but I said already -- and this is my 20th day here, and I'm really anxious to testify to what I know -- whether it was a small group of them or of the 10th Sabotage Detachment or the Bratunac Brigade I really cannot claim with any certainty, but I know, I'm certain, that it was a small group of soldiers of the Republika Srpska army. Just as you say that some people testified otherwise, some people from the Zvornik Brigade told me that a small group, a small platoon, went down to Potocari. In one clip, there is -- we can see General Mladic saying, "And now forward to Potocari." I'm sure you remember that, and I'm certain that what I'm saying is what I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let us -- well, let me ask you. Did you ever tell Mr. Ruez that you did, in fact, see Drina Wolves in and around the Potocari compound? You can give me a "yes" or a "no" answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I mentioned to him the Drina Wolves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's turn to another issue, and that is your testimony that you unilaterally decided to pack up the communications centre on the evening of the 11th of July. Witness DB, at the time you made this decision to pack up the communications centre, the 28th Division and the actual whereabouts of the 28th Division was not known, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 28th Division was a unit that could have done a counter-attack, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Listening to all the information coming from the battlefield and to all the intercepts, radio intercepts, as of 10th of July, we had information that the 28th Division got orders from the Corps to -- 2nd Corps [as interpreted] to concentrate around the UN base, whereas the 28th Division was to prepare for an advance towards Kladanj, so that we -- with all the radio intercepts and all the information we had from the front line told us that the 28th Division was broken up, and that there was no chance of them carrying out a counter-attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive an order from either General Krstic or General Mladic to pack up the mobile communications centre and proceed to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not get such an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me read you the testimony of General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And I'm referring to the testimony of the 19th of October, 2000, page 6196.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I see it's not on the record, but I think the witness had said that the civilians were to concentrate around the UN base in Potocari. That is line 10 or 11. That is not, not the "2nd Corps," but the civilians were to concentrate around the Potocari base, whereas the 28th Division was supposed to prepare a breakthrough. I know it is not important to the testimony now elicited by Mr. Harmon, but it may be important later.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'll stipulate to that. It can be corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, before you will end this, I just have some kind of question. The witness had said to -- and I'm asking Witness DB. You said to Mr. Ruez that it was the Drina Wolves who were among the population, and today you don't seem to be sure. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I told him that, and that there was a small group of those soldiers. And analysing the whole thing later, seeing that Mr. Ruez did not believe me, I asked some people from the Zvornik Brigade, and indeed, they said that one group, one squad, went down -- had gone down to Potocari. And I thought that some of the UN soldiers who had been in that base or someone from that enormous crowd of civilians who come to testify here would confirm what I had said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please proceed, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Riad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me read you the testimony of General Krstic found at 6196 and goes through to 6198. I'm reading from lines 22 to 25 on 6196, and lines 1 through 4 on 6198. "This order --" this is a question by my colleague Mr. Petrusic. "This order concerns both you and General Zivanovic." Actually, I realise I'm going to have to go into private session to read this part of the testimony and examine on it, so if we could do that briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I have a private session just for a few questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, please. Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm focusing your attention now on the meeting that you say occurred on the 11th of July at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, and I'd like to ask you some questions about that. Did you attend the meeting from -- what time did you arrive at the meeting location, and what time did the meeting start?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I arrived at the meeting location around 2200 hours, and I think that immediately after that, the meeting started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you leave the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left about half an hour into the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the meeting still going on when you left, or had it concluded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting, as I said yesterday, in my opinion didn't have a strictly military atmosphere, but all the participants remained in the same room after I left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did -- at that -- I'm sorry. At that meeting, you were ordered to go to establish the forward command post at Krivace; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is your testimony that General Mladic gave you that order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you had to have the agreement of General Mladic -- I'm sorry -- General Krstic, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That agreement was automatically implied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in addition to going to establish the forward command post, was there an order given to carry out a search of the terrain on the following day, on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not present if such an order was issued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell Mr. Ruez that you were present and such an order was issued?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I can't claim that with certainty, because I expected that immediately all units would be regrouped for Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did the participants at that meeting know where the 28th Division elements were located and what were their intentions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that all of them assumed that they were grouped somewhere in the north-western part of the enclave and that they would probably try to break through towards Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at that meeting that you attended, did General Mladic say that, from that moment on, command of all the forces, the Drina Corps forces in the municipalities of Srebrenica, Bratunac, Zvornik, Milici, and Vlasenica, would be assumed by him personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that wording.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, had the command of the Drina Corps units in those municipalities been taken over personally by General Mladic, that implies, does it not, that those units would then report to General Mladic; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In military terms, that would be so. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then that would mean that the -- on the combat reports, for example, and the daily combat reports, those would be sent to General Mladic, as the commander now of the Drina Corps forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you left the meeting, did you leave a signalsman with General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of that signalsman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirko Plakalovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was supposed to provide communications assistance for General Krstic while he remained behind; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He carried with him a mobile device for radio communication with subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the next time you saw this particular signalsman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, though we did discuss it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You discussed what? You mean you discussed this with the signalsman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was discussed? Briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: We discussed his movements after the 11th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did he go after the 11th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: He stayed in Bratunac with General Krstic and he spent the night in Bratunac, that night, and he remembers that after he went with him into the field somewhere where our units were -- but we were unable to establish when he reached Zepa, because he too later was transferred to Zepa. He cannot remember the details -- and I replaced some of the soldiers and gave them leave when moving from Srebrenica to Zepa so that they could rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the signalsman accompany General Krstic to the forward command post at Krivace?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: His recollection is that he just spent the night in Bratunac, the night between the 11th and the 12th, and that during the day he went with him with this equipment into the hills, in the direction of our units, and he doesn't remember whether he reached Krivace with him, or Godjenje, or whether he was transported with the other units that were being transferred to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'd like to turn your attention to the events in Zepa. We're going to focus on Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'd like to have Prosecutor's Exhibit 785, please, shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while we are waiting for the exhibit to be distributed, Witness, at the -- during the Zepa operations, there were three forward command posts during that operation: one at Krivace, one at Godjenje, and one at Zlovrh; is that correct? Z-l-o-r -- Z-l-o-v-r-h. Is that correct? I can't pronounce it, but ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's all right. I'm communicating with the interpreters. That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Now, do Your Honours have a copy of the map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Not right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you could take this exhibit and put it in front of you while the map is being distributed. And you'll see on that map I have highlighted a number of locations, and this is merely to orient us in respect of this campaign. Now, Witness, do you see the location of the forward command post at Krivace? Is that indicated --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you put this on the ELMO first?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can point these locations out to us, please. Witness, do you see the location of Krivace marked on this map, and is that the location of the forward command post that was set up in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The forward command post was here, on this bend in the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So indicating the bend in the road underneath the highlighted word "Krivace," so it's in the general area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you see beneath that a highlighted area with Godjenje, G-o-d-e-n-j-e? It appears at the bottom of the map between the coordinates 47 and 48.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the location of the second forward command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let's go up, Mr. Usher, so we can show -- right there. If you can hold that right there, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the area indicated Veliki Zep? Can you point that out on the map for the Judges?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating the orange-marked area Veliki Zep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Veliki Zep is the location of the repeater from which you could send radio communications from your location at the forward command post up to the Drina Corps headquarters, is that correct, and to the Main Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those were telephone communications using radio relay links.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you also indicated that General Krstic spent the night with his in-laws at a village. Is that the village of Kusace, which is marked on this map in orange?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is the village where General Krstic spent the nights during the Zepa campaign. And Han Pijesak, lastly, is the location of the Main Staff of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Han Pijesak is the location where the Main Staff of the VRS had its headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, 11 kilometres away from Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you locate that for us, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this location here, coloured in dark grey.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Indicating, for the record, the area between the letters "J" and "A" and the word "Javor," that is, northwest of the location Veliki Zep. All right, thank you very much for orienting us with this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm completed with this exhibit, thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, witness, did you receive a copy of the operational plan for the offensive operations in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you -- what time did you arrive in Zepa on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: At about 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did any of the units that were to participate in the offensive operation in Zepa arrive on the 12th of July at the forward command post Krivace or around the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that parts of the 5th Podrinje Infantry Brigade had arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any other units, elements of any other units arrive on the 12th of July in and around the Krivace forward command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember that. All the units were grouping away from Krivace, outside my field of vision, but I know that when I passed by a locality called Plane, that I did see elements of the 5th Podrinje Brigade and that I communicated with their signalsman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any other elements of the attacking group, the other brigades, show up around Plane on the 12th, or did they show up the following day, or do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember only that the other units started arriving in the afternoon and early evening hours of the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know a Drina Corps Commander by the name of Furtula?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Furtula, a Major, he was at the time commander of the 5th Podrinje Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his first name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radomir Furtula.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: For Your Honours' sake, on the organogram, Radomir Furtula appears at this location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did he show up at -- in Zepa to participate in these operations? Did you see him at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of the operation, I would see him at the forward command post. He and his unit took part in the Zepa operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I'm ready for you to decide you have reached the maximum of 70 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have about two more questions, then, that I will have reached my 70-minute limit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know an individual by the name of Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I know Milan Lukic from Visegrad, and as in 1997, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since this is identifying information, the Defence would request a private session for these questions because we still don't know whether he is a soldier, and the witness mentioned the year 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, I'm in a position to clarify that, Your Honour, with a few additional questions, and I'd be glad to do that. I'm not sure a private session is required at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: We try to give safety to all those who are mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, this is an individual who has been mentioned many times in public session in the course of this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Judge Wald?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not that person, it's myself that is at stake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: We're very keen on your safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In that case, I have no objection, in that case, to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good. You go now or you go after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I only have a few questions in this area, so I'd like to proceed now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have no additional questions at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: At this point. How long do you still have to ask questions, to interrogate the witness, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Conservatively, a maximum of two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So if we -- maximum of two hours. I suggest, then, we'll have a break of one hour so that you can have some rest, and then we come back at 2.25 exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But I hope it will not be more than two. The Judges might have some questions, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I hope it won't be more than two as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, it's exceptional for the whole staff, I have to thank them, because the witness has to leave absolutely, I think, by today or tomorrow. And I would like to thank the witness, you have been very cooperative. Thank you very much. We'll come back at 2.25. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.25 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Ms. Registrar, I think you have an announcement to make.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. I have been informed that the interpreters can only work a maximum of five hours and twenty minutes. I've calculated the time thus far, and it's approximately three hours, so therefore we have two hours and twenty minutes. Now, I know Mr. Harmon mentioned two hours, but the Defence also needs 10 minutes, 10 or 15 minutes for redirect, and also I don't know how long the Judges plan to ask questions, but we need to calculate this so that we do not run over the designated time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Krystal. Just a clarification. The two hours, twenty, do not include the break, do they?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just strictly work time in the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So we can still have a break.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, can we request that you give us a quarter of an hour from your two hours?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good. Then we -- and our Defence lawyers need more than a quarter of an hour?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And then we keep 20 minutes for the Judges. Judge Wald?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I don't need 20 minutes, but whatever you need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: We'll have to share them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you. We can start, and we have no -- there will be no chance to continue after that. The witness has to go back home.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. I'll make sure he gets home. He won't be impeded by my examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DB, we're going to try to move through your testimony in order for you to get home. So let me start with -- let me continue in the area we were talking about. We were talking about the Krivace Forward Command Post, and my first question this afternoon is: What time and what date did General Krstic arrive at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly at what time, but I think he -- I think it was the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when did the offensive operation actually commence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it commenced on the 14th, in the morning hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us talk briefly about the communications system that you set up at Krivace. I understood from your previous testimony that it was similar to the communications system that you had set up in Srebrenica, at Pribicevac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at the Krivace Forward Command Post, you could use -- as the means of communication, you could use a teleprinter, a telephone that would convert the conversation into a radio beam that would be transmitted from your location, through Veliki Zep, up in the direction of either the Drina Corps headquarters in Vlasenica or the Main Staff located near Han Pijesak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in respect of those communications, the form of communication that was protected was the teleprinter; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was one of the protected forms of communication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the communications that were directed from the forward command post via Veliki Zep to the Main Staff were protected more than the communications that were directed from your location via Veliki Zep to the Drina Corps headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: They worked according to the same principle. Just a second. Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Were the communications between the Krivace Forward Command Post and Han Pijesak better protected -- did they have more protection than the communications from Krivace to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Excuse me. Our screens have gone blank, our transcript -- oh, okay. Are they okay now? All right. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It's all right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me repeat the question. Did the communications that went from the Krivace Forward Command Post to the Han Pijesak command of the Main Staff have better protection than the communications that went from the Krivace Forward Command Post up to the Drina Corps headquarters in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Teleprinter lines had the same protection system, whereas oral communications over the telephone had a better system of protection towards the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the telephone communications that went toward the main -- I'm sorry, towards Vlasenica headquarters of the Drina Corps were interceptable, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And therefore it was your practice, was it not, to try to avoid important conversations over the telephone between your location and the Drina Corps command in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I always cautioned my superiors, whether their communication is protected or not, whether it can be intercepted or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my point was that the communications that went from over the telephone between your location and the Drina Corps command headquarters in Vlasenica was one where you tried to avoid transmitting, conveying important information because of the fear that those conversations would be intercepted.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean I personally, or you mean all those who used this line?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All those who used the line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would warn in advance about the interceptability of the communication, and whether or not they would include important information in their conversation is something that they decided for themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me have Prosecutor's Exhibit 529 shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll be very brief on this exhibit, Witness DB.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If the English version could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DB, this is an intercepted communication from the 13th of July at 2040 hours, and the identified participants are General Krstic and "X," who is identified as Borovcanin from the specials. Would you review this conversation, please. Do you recognise this conversation? Do you recall this conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Borovcanin from the specials would be the Borovcanin who we talked about yesterday and whose picture I showed you in two exhibits, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. Now, let me --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm finished with this exhibit, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you, you testified that you went from -- you stayed at the forward command post and went -- in Pribicevac, went directly to the forward command post in Zepa. Did you ever leave the forward command post in Krivace and do anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stayed at the forward command post in Krivace about three days, two or three days, from the commencement of combat operations. And then we moved to the forward command post at Godjenje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I did not leave the forward command post at Krivace except perhaps to go to visit a unit which was very nearby before the combat operations began.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after the combat operations began, did you ever return to Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever go take a bath or a shower?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: While we were at Godjenje, I went at least once to have a shower, but that was only after we moved to the forward command post at Godjenje. That means about ten days after the commencement of combat operations, around that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you -- where did you go to take that bath or shower?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the command of the Drina Corps, where my premises were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me ask the Prosecutor's Exhibit 687 be placed on the ELMO, please. Can you place the English on the ELMO? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is an intercept, Witness DB, dated the 18th of July at 2050 hours, and the participants are Krstic and "X," and I'd like you to read that intercept.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said of the 18th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Where is it written the 18th of July?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The evidence has been presented earlier by previous witnesses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, let me direct your attention to --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Actually, could we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: We go into private session. Please tell us when you finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'll repeat what I just said. I'm going to be distributing the next exhibit, or asking that the next exhibit be distributed. It's Prosecutor's Exhibit 765A and B. It's a transcript of a film. And we'll play this film and then I will ask the witness some questions about it. And if we could have Prosecutor's Exhibit 765 played. And Mr. Usher, in the meantime, if you could collect Prosecutor's Exhibit 819/1, 819/2, and 820 to show the witness so we can move this part of the examination quite quickly. Witness, if you'd watch the monitor, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can we stop this for just a minute? I have no audio portion of this part. Could I have the technical booth -- we're supposed to have an audio component to this film, and I'm not getting that and neither are the Judges, and I don't think my colleagues are either, so ... There's a transcript in the meantime, Your Honours. I can either ask that the whole film be replayed or we can pick up the audio portion from this point on.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I've just spoken with the AV section, and he says he's going to get someone to come in and fix it right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Well, we'll show this --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: But it had no audio, is what he said, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Well, they'll have to fix that because it was presented to them with an audio component, and there's a transcript here. But we will view this film in a few minutes when it's fixed. If I could get the signal when it is. And in the meantime, I can go to another part of the examination and we will continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll return to this film in just a minute, Witness DB. Let me turn my attention from Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric to Lieutenant Colonel Cerovic. Now, Lieutenant Colonel Slobodan Cerovic was the chief of the department of moral guidance and legal affairs in the Drina Corps; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you remember when he came down to the forward command post to brief General Krstic about the events that had been taking place in the Drina Corps area of operations outside of the Zepa region? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. During the Zepa operation -- the film I'm going to show you -- first of all, do you recognise what little you've seen of this film to have been filmed in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the course of the Zepa campaign, there were a series of negotiations and ceasefires, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, to the best of your recollection, about the number of times there was a ceasefire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were those ceasefires -- for what duration of time were those ceasefires?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: They lasted several hours or more.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We're getting a report at the moment, Witness, from the audio booth, apparently.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: AV section just informed me that they have the video ready. However, the poor quality -- due to the poor quality of the tape, the audio part is not going to be much better, but they can play it and --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, we are in a position, Your Honours, to provide a quality on this audio that perhaps is better than the one that was submitted. We have taken a transcript from it, but I would like to show Your Honours -- at least pick up the part of the tape where we left off. And what Your Honours will see are negotiations taking place, with General Mladic leading those negotiations, with Lieutenant Colonel Cerovic as a -- when I say "participant," a non-verbal participant in those negotiations. And Your Honours will recall the film footage we have shown Your Honours of the negotiations in the Hotel Fontana on the evening of the 11th and the morning of the 12th, and on the morning of the 12th you will see -- you'll recall that it was General Mladic who was leading those negotiations and his subordinates were silent, and Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric was present at the far end of the table. So we will proceed. If we could have that video now played. Witness DB, that was for your benefit as well, because I'm going to be asking you some questions about this video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: What date did this take place on?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not know the date of this. I know it was sometime during the Zepa operation. It was during one of the ceasefires.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That individual speaking is not from the VRS, he's Ukrainian, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if the witness could be shown a series of photographs or images, still images from the film.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown the images, and if we could start with Prosecutor's Exhibit 820 and place that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DB, the man on the lower right-hand side of the image, with a large moustache and a bald head, who is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Svetozar Kosoric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know either of the two men who are also in this image, either of the two men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard in the conversation at a meeting, so I know roughly who they could be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they military figures, or are they civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at them and by their appearance on this photograph, they are civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next exhibit, which will be Prosecutor's Exhibit 819 -- is there a slash on that? 19/1? We're going to start with 819/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It should be 819/2, and on this image, Witness DB, starting from the far left-hand side, we recognise General Mladic. Can you go from General Mladic's left-hand side and identify the individuals working in the direction of Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric? Let's start with the individual immediately to the left of General Mladic. Can you identify that individual?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, I think this is General Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next individual, to the left of General Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recognise the next two individuals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the individual at the head of the table, again with the handlebar moustache or the large moustache and the bald head, Lieutenant Colonel Kosoric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is he.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, we won't proceed with the next exhibit. Thank you very much. Now, who was leading the negotiations in the Zepa campaign, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, at the place where the negotiations were conducted, General Mladic was there frequently, as well as General Tolimir, and I think that, on one occasion, at least on one occasion, I don't know whether on more occasions, I think General Krstic went there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Lieutenant Colonel Popovic, the head of the Drina Corps security, at the forward command posts in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing him ever there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did General Zivanovic ever appear in Zepa at any of the forward command posts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us why General Zivanovic left the military? Let me ask you this. I'll withdraw that question. Can you tell me why General Zivanovic was relieved of command of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything, soldier talk, as to the reasons why he left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, there was no talk of him being replaced. The talk was that he was going to take up another position in the Main Staff, and there was talk that he was going to retire. But there was no talk that he had been dismissed or relieved of his duties, because just then I think he was promoted to a higher rank so that I cannot infer from that that he was replaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, if the Witness -- if we could get Prosecutor's Exhibits 805 and 780. If you would show the witness the B/C/S version, starting first of all with Prosecutor's Exhibit 805.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DB, these are copies of indictments. The first indictment that I'm going to show you is Prosecutor's Exhibit 805. It is an indictment against Radovan Karadzic and Ratko Mladic that was filed by the Prosecutor of this Tribunal on July 24th, 1995, and was confirmed a day later by a Judge of this Tribunal. Did you hear about the indictment of the Supreme Commander and the head of the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that roughly at the time when forces started the -- the SFOR forces started arriving in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, so those public indictments were hung up together with the names and photographs of the accused so that all of us could see it. And I think there was a poster which had some 50 or 60 accused on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you fix a date for us when you recall becoming aware of the indictment of Radovan Karadzic and Ratko Mladic, when you personally became aware of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hadn't learnt about the indictment, I just learnt from this poster that he had been indicted. This was probably broadcast in the media, but these are reports which did not represent anything particularly new for us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that didn't cause any kind of a sensation amongst the army corps, as far as you are aware?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no particular sensation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you Prosecutor's Exhibit 780, which is the indictment of Radovan Karadzic and Ratko Mladic for the events that took place in Srebrenica. This indictment was filed by the Prosecutor on November the 14th, 1995, and was confirmed two days later by a Judge of this Tribunal. Now, this indictment deals with the very events that are in issue in this trial. Did you hear that the Supreme Commander and the head of the army had been indicted for the mass execution of thousands of Muslim men and boys that occurred in and around the Srebrenica enclave, specifically within the Drina Corps area of responsibility? Did you hear about this indictment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that they had been indicted of war crimes. What kind of war crime and the details, I had no precise knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher, I'm finished with those exhibits.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did members of the VRS execute thousands of Bosnian Muslim men and boys in and around Srebrenica in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information that I heard from the radio, television, and the press, and during the preparations for my testimony here, it appears that it is without doubt the truth that this crime that you have described occurred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me turn to another part of your testimony, and specifically --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Wait for the transcript. What's wrong with the transcript? Just a second, we have to -- do you have transcript? Good. We don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We're receiving transcript from the Prosecutor's bench, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Do you have it? Do you have the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Riad, we have a transcript that is appearing for our bench, at least on my monitor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Can we let him continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I'm okay because I can understand him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You can continue; we understand your English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: But we don't understand the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: That also comes back in translation. It's back, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right, we have surmounted our technical difficulties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you -- actually, let me turn your attention to part of your testimony that took place, I believe it was the day before yesterday or yesterday. My colleague, Mr. Petrusic, asked you the following questions, and you gave the following response. And I'm referring to the LiveNote of July the -- I'm sorry -- November the 7th, page 7093 to the following page, and I'm reading from lines 15 to 25, and then on the following page, 1 through 9. My colleague, Mr. Petrusic, asked you the following questions and you gave the following answers: "Q. Do you know what position General Krstic held in the command of the Drina Corps on the 13th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that General Krstic was the Chief of Staff of the Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to when General Krstic became commander of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that this is an important question, but in my preparations for my testimony here, I read the order of the President of the Republika Srpska, dated 15th of July, appointing General Krstic commander of the Drina Corps, because it is only the president who has the authority to appoint people who -- these strategic groupings and positions. While we were at Zepa, whether it was over the media or in some other way, any way, we learnt of the decree of the President of the Republic, and I know that sometime around the 20th of July, or thereabouts, there was a gathering of generals in a facility close to Han Pijesak. There were a number of generals from the Main Staff and the commanders of the other corps, and also present with General Zivanovic and General Krstic. And I know that the event was organised to observe the handover of duty by the commander of the Drina Corps, and I know that after General Krstic's return to the forward command post in the village of ..." And I'm assuming this is Krivace or Godjenje. There's nothing indicated on my transcript. "... some people congratulated him on his taking over of duty." Now, I've concluded my reading of your answer, and from your answer it appears that you have based your opinion first on the decree of President Karadzic, about which you learned sometime while you were in Zepa. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also base your opinion on -- you also state that you knew sometime around the 20th of July there was a meeting where the formal handover took place, handover ceremony between General Zivanovic and General Krstic; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, lastly, you say that there were some people who congratulated General Krstic when he returned to the forward command post on his taking over duty. Now, let me ask you: In respect of the information that you learned in preparation for your testimony, when was it that you first saw the actual document appointing General Krstic as the commander that confirmed what you had actually heard while you were in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Six or seven days ago; five, six, seven days ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you personally attend the meeting where the handover ceremony took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you identify for us the individuals who congratulated General Krstic at the forward command post when he returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the individuals by name, but I know that the atmosphere was such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let me then -- in respect of the decree of the president. You've told us in the course of your testimony that there were formalities in law and in regulations. Let me give you some examples of what I mean. You testified in respect of the formal elements of a communications plan, there were certain identifiable elements that, by regulation, were required, but because of wartime conditions, the rules and regulations were not strictly adhered to. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that there was no official designation in a numerical sense for the identification of commanders at various headquarters. For example, you said wartime conditions resulted in the designations being 01, 02, and that wasn't strictly in accordance with the regulations. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's fair to say that in this war, while there were regulations and there were rules, wartime conditions often resulted in a deviation from those rules and regulations; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you have seen this document that is a document that appoints General Krstic as the commander, and in the strict formal sense, there are certain things that have to follow, and you've told us about those elements. But wartime conditions oftentimes don't require that every rule and every regulation be followed, and that includes, does it not, the appointment of officers to command positions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you in the most part, Mr. Prosecutor, but I think that a presidential decree, after all, is a decree by the president.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that there was a presidential decree and the presidential decree was required for a number of positions, officer positions, but can you allow for the possibility that de facto someone assumes command prior to the issuance of a piece of paper signed by the president which formally designates the individual to a command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I accept that possibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me read to you --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Actually, I need to go into private session for just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Ms. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me read to you a question -- actually, let me withdraw that question. The following answer that I'm going to read to you was an answer that was volunteered by you and not directly responsive to the question that was asked. So let me read this to you. "MR. RUEZ: Do you know if he returned to the Drina Corps headquarters during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that it was a ceremony to mark when General Zivanovic landed -- it should be handed -- over his duties as Corps Commander to him, and I think that day he was in the corps headquarters. I heard the story that that was on the 13th. I don't know the exact date, but I think it happened at the beginning of the operation in Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUEZ
utterances.text: And what is, for you, the beginning of the operation on Zepa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
