utterances.text: If I follow the chronology on dates, I think that beginning of the attack on Zepa was 14th, because on the 12th, Krstic wasn't there. On 13th, the units were collecting ... were actually gathering, so it sounds logical to me that we attacked on Zepa on 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUEZ
utterances.text: Okay. So do you remember 13th of July, at what moment of the day did General Krstic arrive to Krivace?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't. He had the handover of duties in Drina Corps, so it was probably late in the evening, but I know for sure that he wasn't there on the 12th, but he was there when the attack was launched." Let me read on. "Q. You heard about the ceremony of passing over of the command between General Zivanovic and General Krstic that you believe happened on 13th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: During preparations for this interview, I was told that it took place on 13th. At the time, I knew it happened, but I cannot recall exact day, but I know it actually happened at the beginning of the attack on Zepa. And I knew that many questions are asked that relate to that very date. The debates are related to that date. Most probably they want to clarify who commander of responsibility at the time, whether that was covered by the order and somebody's signature, or handover before the most important officers. I don't know anything personally about that, so I don't have any kind of judgement about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUEZ
utterances.text: Okay, you said `in preparation for this interview.' Could you develop on this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I obtained the information. For instance, as for Srebrenica, you know, I didn't know the exact date we entered Srebrenica. I thought that we entered Srebrenica on the 12th, and later I found out it was on the 11th, and therefore I use that as that date. For instance, in talks with some other soldiers or officers who were at Zepa, I know I asked, `I know that General Krstic wasn't present there the very first day,' and I know that some of them said that that handover took place on the 13th." Witness, were you asked those questions by Mr. Ruez, and did you provide those answers to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, which officers did you talk to prior to this interview that led you to this position? Can you identify them for us, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that interview, I spoke to my signalsman, wishing to establish the chronology of events. I may have also spoken to Colonel Andric or some other officers who are still in the army of Republika Srpska. I mentioned some officers yesterday whose names I remember that I spoke to for us to try and ascertain the chronology of events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was it these officers who provided you with the information that the handover of command between General Zivanovic and General Krstic took place prior to the commencement of the operation in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my answer that you have just read out and which I provided on the 4th of April, it can be seen that I provided that answer on the basis of the conversations I had with certain people up to that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question, Witness DB, was, did General Andric, who was then a colonel and who was later to become General Krstic's Chief of Staff in the Drina Corps, was he one of the individuals who informed you that the pass-over of command from General Zivanovic to General Krstic occurred prior to the commencement of the Zepa operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke to him. I cannot remember the conversation in detail, but I wanted to learn the truth and to see whether my testimony was correct. So subsequently, I was informed of a date sometime around the 20th of July when the gathering of all Generals was held, when something like the handover took place, and I was also subsequently informed of the decree of the president of the republic, dated the 15th of July. So in the strictly military sense, I reach the conclusion that the official handover could have taken place after the 15th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was still not answered. Witness DB, when you prepared for this interview on April the 4th with representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor, you informed Mr. Ruez that you had conversed with a number of officers and soldiers in the Drina Corps who had informed you that the official pass-over ceremony of command between General Zivanovic and General Krstic occurred prior to the commencement of the Zepa operation. My question is very simple. Will you identify for us, please, the officers, by name, who told you that the transition in command in the Drina Corps took place before the commencement of the Zepa operation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you the names of those people, not because I don't want to, because I can't remember which officers by name conveyed to me such an opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did General Andric convey such an opinion to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't present on the 13th, and I think he wasn't there on the 20th, either, but I'm almost quite sure that he wasn't present on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That wasn't the question I asked. My question was, did he tell you that General Krstic took over command from General Zivanovic prior to the start of the Zepa operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Major Obrenovic, who you identified as an individual with whom you spoke, did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Lieutenant Colonel Vicic tell you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did speak to Vicic, and I do assume that he might have told me about that because, at the time, he could have been close to the events in question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was, as you earlier described, General Krstic's number two de facto?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Correct. Now, since this interview was a very important interview, as you've said, please tell me who told you. Try to refresh your recollection. Take some time and tell me who told you this information that the pass-over of command took place prior to the commencement of the Zepa operation. Take a minute, reflect.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't need time. I told you in answer to your question that it is a very difficult question because I'm not sure. I cannot tell you with certainty what applies to the 13th, what to the 15th, and what to the 30th of July in the legislative sense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm certainly not interested in the legislative sense, I'm interested who told you that the handover took place prior to the Zepa operation. The legislative sense we have dealt with.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, I have no objection, Your Honour, because the witness has already answered that. This is the third or fourth time that the Prosecutor is repeating the same question and getting the same answer, but before my objection the witness gave his answer, so I withdraw that objection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've been here, Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: When will we finish this line of questions? Because we have to have a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm going to say five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: All right. These are exceptional circumstances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, this information that you have provided to the Trial Chamber under oath is entirely different than the information that you provided to the Office of the Prosecutor seven months ago, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have been in The Hague for 20 days. Did you make any attempt to contact the Office of the Prosecutor to inform them of this new information that you had developed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I think that the information does not and the data does not different significantly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to talk to General Krstic in the past seven months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to see his publicly-broadcasted statement that he made to the Office of the Prosecutor that was part of this trial?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In summary form, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you review -- well, in summary form. What do you mean by "in summary form"? Explain that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I saw consisted of some 30 pages, and when they gave this to us, that the whole interview consists of about 90 pages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave you the 30-page summary of the interview?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did they give that to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: A month and a half or two months ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have no additional questions in this line of inquiry. I only have one additional line of inquiry after the recess, and it shouldn't take that long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So we'll have a recess for 20 minutes, come back at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Before we proceed, Mr. Harmon, we have, I think, something like an hour and 20 minutes -- no, an hour and 10 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Judge Riad, I'll finish in my allotted time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: We'll need for the redirect a quarter of an hour and for the Judges 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I will go through these documents as quickly as I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I, for one, am going to -- I'm ready to give you -- to grant you my part of questions, which is 10 minutes, but I don't know if the redirect will do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I think I can finish very quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could start with Prosecutor's Exhibit 463. Mr. Usher, if you'd show the witness the B/C/S version of this document, then place the English version on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DB, have you seen this document before testifying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it a couple of days ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, so you -- I don't have to have you read this whole document. You're somewhat familiar with this document, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document that is issued on the 13th of July, from the command of the Drina Corps, and it is signed by whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see in front of me a very bad copy, but I think this is General Krstic's signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the title, the position under which General Krstic's signature appears?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "Commander."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this appears to be an order issued by the commander of the Drina Corps on the 13th of July, 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And under the -- at the caption at the top, "strictly confidential," it has number 01. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does 01 signify?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the sense it is used here, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it have any significance in the sense that it's in this order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember the rules, in the instructions on office work, this first number should denote either the command or an organ within the command. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I don't need to spend much time on that aspect of this document. This document -- you've seen it before -- is an order issued by General Krstic, as commander, to the commands of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, the 1st Milici Light Infantry Brigade, and the Skelani Independent Battalion, to conduct search operations in the area of Srebrenica. So this is an order that is issued by him that is outside the immediate theatre of the operation in Zepa; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that these units took part in the Zepa operation, but from the north side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you, Witness: This document, signed by General Krstic as the commander, is consistent with the information that you provided to Mr. Ruez in your interview on the 4th of April, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let's turn to the next document, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 464. And in the meantime, to the registrar, if we could get prepared Prosecutor's Exhibit 536, 537.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You should have before you Prosecutor's Exhibit 464. Have you seen this document before testifying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document that is issued on the 14th of July, 1995, on the basis of the previous order that you have just seen that was issued by General Krstic as the commander, and this has been issued by Colonel Vidoje Blagojevic. Now, this document is a document that has been issued based on the commander's order. It was issued by General Krstic; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could turn to Prosecutor's Exhibit 536. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take just a moment to look at that document. Witness DB, this is a document that is a daily combat report that was issued by the command of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade on the 15th of July, 1995, and it was sent to the command of the Drina Corps, as well as the IKM, the forward command post of the Drina Corps. And if I can direct your attention to paragraph 2 in this document, you will see that again this makes reference to the order issued Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. by General Krstic as the commander, and it says that, "Our forces are still searching the terrain in accordance with your strictly confidential order number 01/4-157/5, dated 13 July 1995." Now, this is a combat report that has been sent directly to the commander of the Drina Corps pursuant to the order that was issued by him previously. I see my colleague is on his feet, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence objects. Referring to this order, the one we see on the ELMO, Mr. Harmon said this was an order making reference, saying that this order was issued by the commander, but in the quoted paragraph 2, it doesn't say "commander" anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, I fully agree with my colleague, but it makes reference to order 01/4-157/5 which is the order, Prosecutor's Exhibit 463, which is the order that was issued by General Krstic as the commander of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Would you like to add anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all right, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This, in very short form, Witness DB, is the subordinate commander responding to the commander pursuant to an order that was issued to him, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's turn to Prosecutor's Exhibit 537A. Have you seen this document before testifying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's then identify the individuals in the upper left-hand corner. This document was sent by Colonel Ignjat Milanovic who, I believe, was the corps air defence officer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's dated the 15th of July, 1995, and it's directed to the forward command post, attention of the commander. And in the first paragraph, it references specifically "your orders," referring to, presumably, the commander. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It refers to the person from whom he had received the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And the addressee at the forward command post is identified as the commander, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the 15th, General Zivanovic was not at the forward command post, was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should like to clarify one thing. Every forward command post has its own commander. A forward command post is a temporary composition consisting of units which are temporarily engaged for an operation, and the command which was at the forward command post at Pribicevac or the forward command post in Zepa, this forward command post would have its own commander. So it's quite possible that this enactment of Colonel Milanovic was addressed to the commander of the corps' forward command post. Did you understand me? The Corps Commander does not necessarily have to be always at the forward command post. The forward command post can be commanded by his deputy or the operations officer or a third person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the first addressee on this document is the person identified as the commander at the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this document deals with the subject matter of searching the terrain that was found in the previous exhibit, 463, the order issued by General Krstic, commander of the Drina Corps, on the 13th of July, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Colonel Milanovic has ordered, in number two, he says, "The assignment you have given to the commanders, to be carried out without fail." So this is a reference back to the commander, and it is a proposal that you will see at the end of the document, asking the commander, if you agree with the proposal, to take certain actions. Now, given the context of this document, Witness DB, to whom do you think this document was directed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was directed to the three addressees indicated in the right-hand corner of the page, that is, to the commander of the forward command post of the corps, to the corps command, and to the -- to these two units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But the reference in the text is to an individual. In accordance with "your" orders, the assignment "you" have given the commanders, if "you" agree with the proposal. Who do you think the "you" is in this document in light of the other documents that you have seen? Do you think this document was being issued -- was being sent to the commander of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person who had issued that order, and it doesn't say here which order is made reference to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General Krstic, in his testimony in respect of this document, indicated that the individual who was at the forward command post and who was the commander at that location was himself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll move on from this document, and let me show you Prosecutor's Exhibit 469.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And Madam Registrar, if we could have next in order 472, 478, 652.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document, Witness, that was provided to the Office of the Prosecutor by the Republika Srpska Ministry of Defence, and this is the decision to relieve General Zivanovic of the post of commander of the Drina Corps. Now, you have, I think, before you two documents in B/C/S. Am I correct? And if you could put the first document ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is the cover letter that accompanied this document, and you will see, Your Honours, that this is precisely what I said: This is the decision to relieve General Zivanovic of the post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you could turn to the actual document itself, which is a document -- it is the document that is the decree number 1-1419/95, and this document was -- indicates that General Zivanovic was placed on disposal of the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska army, and that he was heretofore the commander of the Drina Corps, and that he is made available for appointment from the 15th of July, 1995. Can you comment on this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to Prosecutor's Exhibit 472A. This is an intercept from the 15th of July. Now, this is a document that -- have you seen this document before, Witness DB?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you can see that, on the 15th of July, at 0954 hours, the participants in this document are General Zivanovic and Colonel Ljubo Beara. And I will read you part of this document, and it says essentially, from Beara, "You know that day, I informed the commander about it, Furtula didn't send Lukic's intervention platoon." Further down, Beara says, "He simply doesn't give a damn about what the commander orders him to do. Well, now, that platoon has 60 men." There is an inaudible portion by General Zivanovic. Beara says: "Have him send at least half. Zivanovic: Yes, yes. Beara: Say again? Zivanovic: To send them immediately. Beara: Yes. Zivanovic: I can't decide that any more." Witness, why couldn't General Zivanovic, if he was the commander of the Drina Corps, decide to send a subordinate unit to a specific location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not claim decidedly that he was Corps Commander then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But is it not consistent, this response by General Zivanovic, that he couldn't order a subordinate unit, isn't that consistent with him no longer being the Corps Commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, as long as he cannot order something to be done by his subordinate units, then he's no longer commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, further down in this document, Beara says -- let me read on. "I can't decide that any more. Beara: Uh-huh. Zivanovic: 385. Beara: 385." Zivanovic is inaudible. Beara again: "385. Zivanovic: That's right. Beara: And that is, what telephone exchange is 385? Zivanovic: Zlatar and 385 V. Beara: Uh-huh, Zlatar. Zivanovic: And stay on the line. Beara: Uh-huh. Zivanovic: And ask for extension 385." Now, Zlatar, we know, is the command of the Drina Corps and 385 is a number that you're familiar with as being one of the exchanges at the Drina Corps command; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the numbers of switchboards, because they changed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next intercept, which is an intercept of the same day that occurred six minutes later, and that is Exhibit 478. You have seen the companion exhibit. You commented on this during your direct examination. It was OTP Exhibit 477A. Let me draw your attention in this intercept to the participants. One is Colonel Ljubo Beara and the other participant is General Krstic. So again, in context, this is six minutes after the phone call that was intercepted earlier that we just talked about. And Beara starts the conversation: "General, Furtula didn't carry out the boss's order. Krstic: Listen, he ordered him to lead out a tank, not a train. Beara: But I need 30 men just like it was ordered. Krstic: Take them from Nastic or Blagojevic, I can't pull anybody out of here for you." Now, I want to pause at this point on this exhibit. Remember in Prosecutor's Exhibit 477 you were asked the question in respect of that exhibit, who is Tasic, and did you know Sladojevic, and you answered that you did not know who those individuals are. Do you know who Nastic is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is Nastic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nastic was, in that period, commander of the Milici Brigade, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was commander of the 1st Bratunac Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were commanders of units that were participating in the Zepa operation, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their units took part in the Zepa operation from the north part, from the direction of Podravanje towards Zepa. I remember that period. Due to the configuration of terrain, we were not able to communicate with them, but Colonel Ignjat Milanovic was designated to coordinate the attack from that direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in this intercept, you can see that -- I'm sorry -- in the previous intercept, General Zivanovic could not order individuals be taken, and in this order, General Krstic apparently has the ability to order individuals who are subordinate commanders to provide men; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from this, can you draw the conclusion that General Krstic was now the commander? Is this intercept consistent with the information that you told Mr. Ruez on April the 4th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this conversation, whether Krstic was commander, if this conversation took place on the 15th. We see from this that it is probably him who decides about this request [as interpreted]. I haven't read this till the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Please take your time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, what is the date of this conversation?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: 15th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this is a document that is consistent --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, page 114, line 7, the witness said that he is probably the one who decides or who could decide, so I think this second part of the phrase was left out. It says "probably him who decides," but the words "who could decide" should also be added, or perhaps Mr. Harmon could repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm satisfied with that addition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: This is already an addition. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DB, this is consistent with General Krstic having the ability to command subordinate units; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be seen from this that he appears to have had that possibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is consistent with what you told Mr. Ruez on the 4th of April in your interview with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told him that I wasn't sure that I had heard stories about that handover of duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me put it this way: It's consistent with the stories that you heard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn to the next Exhibit, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 652. This is an intercepted communication from the 17th of July, and it occurred at 0910 hours in the morning. Have you seen this intercept?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me -- this is -- the participants in this intercept are X; Bedem, the code name, which is the Sarajevo-Romanija Brigade; Krstic; and Veletic. And I will start at the top: "Hello, is that Bedem?" That was X. "B: Yes. X: Listen Bedem, I need to talk to Colonel Veletic. B: I hear that for the first time, believe me." K, which is Krstic: "Bedem, Zlatar 01 here, do you hear me? Over." Now, let me stop right there. 01, you have previously testified, "Zlatar 01" would mean the commander of the Drina Corps; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or the person who is a commander at any command post. He could be the commander of the forward command post, who was the number-one man for that provisional unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's continue on on this intercept and we might be able to clarify this further. "B: Bedem speaking, go ahead. K: Give me Colonel Veletic from your IKM 3, your forward command post. Hold on a moment. K: Krstic here." Now, further down in this, it talks about, from Krstic: "Listen Bedem. General Krstic is calling. B: Yes? Krstic: Tell Veletic I ordered that Lieutenant Colonel Vlacic urgently return to the unit." Now, Witness DB, it appears from the context of this intercept that "Zlatar 01" is Krstic. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, "Bedem" is the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. We established that earlier today; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know an individual named Veletic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Veletic was the man who was on -- I'm sorry -- there was a special group of soldiers that were assigned to the Trnovo area, and Veletic was the commander of those groups; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is it common and ordinary for a commander at a forward command post to issue these kinds of orders to a unit that is attached to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps or is this consistent with an order that was issued by the commander of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether I understood you correctly. You asked me whether it is all right for Zlatar 01 to issue orders to units which are now under the command of Bedem, that is, the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question, so we understand the context: Is this order that is issued consistent with the -- an order issued by the commander of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Trnovo operation was taking place far away from the Zepa area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Krstic was commanding, or at least -- commanding the operation in the Zepa area; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this kind of an order that you see General Krstic giving to an attached unit consistent with the order given by the commander of the Drina Corps in his role as the commander of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Harmon, perhaps it would be best that the term "consistent with" could be replaced with some kind of a military term or another word that would be more readily understandable.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much for the suggestion. What we will do is we will move off of this document and we will move to the next document, 481, Prosecutor's 481. Could you place the English version on the ELMO and ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very quickly, Witness, I'm sure you have seen this document before, have you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that you will see for yourself that for my eyes it is quite unusable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Let me see -- I have a more usable copy, and you can certainly use my copy. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document that is dated the 17th of July, issued from the Drina Corps command, and it is an order, and it is signed by General Krstic. And in what capacity does he sign this order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here in the capacity of Corps Commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, have you had the experience where the document is signed on a certain date and not transmitted for a number of days thereafter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this did occur for the documents that were not marked as being urgent or operational, so there were such cases. Even now, documents that are not urgent can wait to be dispatched for several days, and to be delivered only then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is this document marked urgent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say so anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is this a document that was prepared at the Drina Corps command? Let me assist you. It may assist you if you turn to the last page and you take a look at a set of initials that are at the end of the text. Do you see the initials RJ/LJP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: RJ is the person who prepared the order, and LJP is the typist, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this -- is RJ Lieutenant Colonel Radenko Jovicic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be because the subject matter in the heading fits within the terms of reference of Lieutenant Colonel Jovicic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Lieutenant Colonel Radenko Jovicic ever in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who LJP is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: LJP is one of the ladies working in the typing office, one of the typists in the pool of the command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there ever a female typist at the forward command post in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where do you conclude, or can you conclude, therefore, where this document originated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably in the corps command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me turn to another document. It's Prosecutor's Exhibit 476.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, you have to give us some information because you are almost at the end of the five hours 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have four documents to go, and I'm -- I will be -- four documents, and I want to ask then the witness one or two additional questions after that. I'm trying to go through these documents as quickly as I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I'll have to request the interpreters to be kind with us today.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I would appreciate that. Thank you very much, Judge Riad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you interpreters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to show you Prosecutor's Exhibit 467. This -- and if you could place the English on the ELMO. This is a document dated the 17th of July, 1995. It has been issued by the Vidoje Blagojevic, the commander of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, and it references a previous order dated the 14th of July, 1995, and it is informing the corps of the Drina Corps -- I mean the command of the Drina Corps, that representatives of the Bratunac Brigade will attend the official farewell for General Zivanovic who was hitherto the commander of the Drina Corps. And it identifies a going-away party date or a party -- I'm sorry, an occasion on the 23rd of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mentioned a document dated the 17th, Mr. Prosecutor. I don't have that document in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you should have a handwritten document. Your hand is on it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it's dated the 14th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, then. You probably have a very poor copy, but if you take a look at the very poor copy of the document, you'll see in the upper left-hand corner where the date is a "17." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be the 17th. It cannot be seen very clearly, but I suppose you can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, this -- whether it's the 14th or whether it's the 17th, it says that General Zivanovic was hitherto the commander of the Drina Corps. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me turn to Prosecutor's Exhibit 679.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have only two other exhibits after this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This, Witness DB, is an intercept of the 18th of July at 7.16 in the morning. The participants are Krstic and Cerovic. Now, Cerovic was Slobodan Cerovic who was the head of the department of moral guidance and legal affairs in the Drina Corps, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in this order -- this is an order that you can see -- or this is an intercept that relates to an order to deploy Colonel Cerovic and to take command of part of a unit or a unit. He's to deploy to a certain location, and it is General Krstic informing the Cerovic that he's in charge in whatever area he's been designated. Let me ask you, first of all, did Colonel Cerovic come down to Zepa to command any aspect of the operation in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this intercept deals with an order by General Krstic to a subordinate member of the corps branch to assume command in an area outside the Zepa area of responsibility, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the kind of an order that would be given by a commander of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn to Prosecutor's Exhibit 364 and 394 [sic]. These exhibits deal in part, Witness DB, with the situation that was occurring in Trnovo, which, as we all have heard, was outside -- was in the area of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And Mr. Usher, if we could start with 364, 19 July -- let me start with 364/19, tab 1. It is an intercept that is timed, in the upper left-hand corner, at 8.07. And if you would like to use my copy, I have a B/C/S copy, we can ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, what is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Three -- I have a copy, I will provide it to the -- it's 364/19 July, tab 1, but I will give the witness the B/C/S version of my copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And let me ask you, have you seen this interview -- I'm sorry, this intercept?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I haven't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take a moment to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: May I approach the ELMO and place the English version of this on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, have you had an opportunity to read this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. As far as I have been able to grasp this message in view of the legibility of the handwriting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was an intercept that was taken on the 19th of July at 0807 hours, and the correspondents are Colonel Cerovic and Major Eskic, and the context of this is the rotation of men in the area of Trnovo. And I will read one sentence of this. Colonel Cerovic -- this is a summary of the intercept operator. Colonel Cerovic tells him there is a commander's order about that and says, and then there's an exact quote, and that refers to rotating men up at Trnovo. And at the end of this intercept, it says, "I'll call Vinko right away and I'll call you. I'll call the General down there." Now, let me show you the next exhibit, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 694, which is related to this intercept. It is the conversation that occurs five minutes later that is intercepted. This is -- Witness DB, I'll give you an opportunity to look at this, and I'm going to direct you to a certain part of it, but this was a conversation that was intercepted five minutes later, and the correspondents are Colonel Cerovic and Vinko. And Vinko is Vinko Pandurevic who is the commander of the Zvornik Brigade, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'd like to direct your attention to -- why don't you take a quick look at that intercept. It's a long intercept, and I want to direct your attention to a portion of it. Do you see the portion where it starts out, "Well, I know that was the order, that you sent ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is on page 2, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Well, I know that was the order, that you've sent a report, however, this Eskic has just called me from up there and said that he was yesterday somewhere at your place and that he heard you are doing a shift rotation." Do you see that part in the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I do, though this was handwriting by the intercepter, and it is very hard to read.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. Let me read on from that. That was -- the portion I read was Cerovic. "Vinko: No. I did a rotation shift at Nisici. Cerovic: I'm telling you, the report he sent there's not way it can be done ... That's Krstic's order, there are no shift rotations until further notice. Vinko: It would be best if we transfer our complete Corps to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. Cerovic: Yeah, that would be best. Vinko: No, seriously, I've sent you a report yesterday. You could see what kind of losses we sustained. Cerovic: Yes and I presented that to Krstic and wrote him special/report/based on your interim and daily reports. Vinko: Yes, That's correct." Now, I want to go back to the section that says, "That's Krstic's order, there are no shift rotations until further notice." Witness DB, this deals with shift rotations of the Drina Corps elements that were attached to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps fighting around the area of Trnovo. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it refers to those events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the order that there would be no shift rotations is consistent with an order that would be issued by the commander of the Drina Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, whoever is competent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that concludes my examination of this document, Witness DB. I want to ask you -- touch on one additional subject. Yesterday my colleague showed you OTP Exhibit 789, which is a transcript from a tape recording of an intercept. Now, let me show you this Prosecutor's Exhibit 789. You've seen this because you testified about this the other day. It references cowboys. Do you remember that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to listen to the tape recording from which this transcript was prepared?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any voices on that tape recording?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot assert with certainty, because out of the three, two participants can be heard very poorly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of those voices sound familiar to you, even given that they were faint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness DB. I've concluded my examination. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. Mr. Petrusic, you are entitled to a reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it will be far briefer than the amount of time we thought we would need. Re-examined by Mr. Petrusic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DB, I should like to go back to Exhibit 481.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher for his assistance to place it on the ELMO, please, 481.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Give us a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence will put the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DB, this is an order issued on the 17th of July, 1995. Will you please look at the last page. Is there a stamp of the military post office box Zvornik on the back of one of the pages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the incoming stamp when this was received on the 17th of July, 1995 [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was received by the military post code of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible that -- we know that the day when it was typed out was the 17th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think in line 23 there is an error, page 126, line 2. It says the incoming stamp was of the 17th of July. Actually, the date is the 23rd of July -- 24th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes, we can see that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the incoming stamp on this document is of the 24th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The day when it was typed out is the 17th of July? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said this document was not urgent.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible that between these two dates, the 17th and the 24th of July, this document was actually signed by General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you do not exclude -- rule out the possibility that this document could have been signed after the 17th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the usher's assistance, I would like to take Exhibit 463, 464, and 537 -- 536 and 537, and please prepare 464, 536 and 537.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is an order signed by General Krstic, issued on the 13th of July, 1995. Below the word "order" in the first paragraph, General Krstic issues the order to the 1st Bratunac Brigade to carry out a ground search of the former enclave of Srebrenica. So will you please read out the location of this ground search.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the line Ravni Buljim/excluded/Zvijezda/elevation 906/Siljato Brdo/Slapovici, along the Zeleni Jadar River Bank up to Zeleni Jadar bridge/excluded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next Exhibit is 464, and that is an order by Colonel Blagojevic. Did Colonel Blagojevic refer in this order to the order which was quoted a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the location of the ground search identical to the order to which he refers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next exhibit is 536. While this exhibit is still on the ELMO, please look at the order given to subordinate units by Colonel Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, so the terrain which should be searched.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are the features designated by Colonel Blagojevic identical to the features?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit 536. Will you please put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DB, the previous order, which was Exhibit 464, in the first paragraph -- do you have that order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the first paragraph, below the word "order," the assignment is given to search the terrain on the location of Bratunac, Konjevic Polje, and so on. My question was: In the order of General Krstic dated the 13th of July, which was Exhibit 463, does this order refer to the location of Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I apologise, Mr. Petrusic. Perhaps fatigue is taking its toll. There is no reference to the features. The features that were to be searched were designated by General Krstic, and it is not the same as the ones referred to by the commander of the 1st Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the commander of the 1st Bratunac Brigade departs from the order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he does. I know this area very well, and he is actually mentioning a territory, a piece of land entirely on a different side of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will move on to Exhibit 536. I would again refer you to the paragraph 2 of this order. And in view of the order issued on the 13th of July, Exhibit 463 and Exhibit 536, are the locations of ground search identical?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in this case as well we have a deviation from what is written in the order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next exhibit is 537. My question is the same with reference to this exhibit, 537. Is the assignment determined by Colonel Milanovic, referring to General Krstic's order, which was Exhibit 463, identical to this original assignment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it does not correspond to the order of General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is a departure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is a departure. It is a completely different activity to the one defined by General Krstic in his order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And towards the bottom, towards the end of this order of the Exhibit 463, you spoke about the commander of the forward command post. Do you allow the possibility that this signature was made in that capacity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: This possibility exists.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness DB. Mr. President, the Defence has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrusic. Judge Wald, would you like to ask a question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Witness, I have only one question to ask you. Early on, you talked about the period between the time that a commander is appointed and the time when he actually assumes the duties. This is a period eventuating in a handover ceremony of some sort and then he assumes the functions of his new post; is that right? I mean, that is what I thought you were talking about early on in your testimony when you talked about the difference between his being appointed by the President Karadzic's decree and the -- whatever time the ceremony took place in the restaurant with all of the other generals. My only question to you is: Do you know whether or not that notion of the handover being necessary before somebody takes on the duties of the new post, is that actually in a regulation someplace in the VRS manual or regulations, or is it more in the domain of a kind of custom, military custom? I mean, have you ever seen such a regulation? I don't expect you to know it off the top of your head, but do you ever remember reading such a regulation which says there shall be such a ceremony and the person will not assume the duties of his new office until that ceremony has been completed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ceremony is prescribed, I think, in the rules of the service of the Republika Srpska army, and it is titled "Handover of Duty," handover/takeover of duty. Briefly, it implies that, in front of a lined-up unit, the old commander and the new commander should come, accompanied by someone from the superior command, preferably a commander who is elder to them, and then there are other parts of the ceremony which are less important. It is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I wasn't so much interested in the details of the ceremony as the fact that -- is it left completely to the new commander about to be and the old commander who is taking leave, is it up to them to set whatever kind of date they want? I mean, they could make it a week, they could make it a month, there's no set time; it's just up to them to decide when they actually want to pass command along?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one who orders such a pass-over duty, he also prescribes the time frame within which it has to take place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Who would that, who would that be? Because here we have President Karadzic saying that the appointment will be effective on the decree July 15th. So who would then decide, no, we're not going to have a takeover ceremony until the 20th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, since it is the position of Corps Commander, the commander of the Main Staff should write a document which would briefly say, based on the decree of the president of the Republic dated such and such date regarding the appointment of General Krstic as the new commander of Drina Corps, effect the takeover of duty to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Did you ever see such a document in this case, or do you know whether any such document was drawn up by anybody in this particular case when General Zivanovic gave up the position to General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see that document, and I asked counsel Petrusic whether he had that document because that document is tale-telling. He answered that neither the Prosecutor or the Defence were able to find that document which would explain a lot. And that document had to be drafted because it is only on the basis of that document that somebody could have become commander of the corps and receive all the benefits and prerogatives, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Well, my final question on this is, just suppose -- I'm just trying to understand the system -- just suppose between the time that the president appointed General Krstic and said it was effective as of July 15th, suppose something happened to General Zivanovic. Suppose he disappeared, or he was injured in some way so that he simply was out of the picture. You don't mean to say that General Krstic couldn't take over the duties without General Zivanovic being there to hand them over in that case, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: He not only could not have taken over that duty, he had to take it over in that kind of situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So in that kind of situation, the practicalities, the exigencies would rule, right, because it was wartime? Okay, thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Wald. Witness DB, I want to make sure that I understood one of your statements right. In one of the answers to -- in the cross-examination of Prosecutor, you said that the chain of command in the Srebrenica operation was intact. That's what I got. And then afterwards you're speaking about Mladic ordering you to establish the forward command post of Krivace after the meeting at 22 hours at night. And also when you were asked about General Krstic approval, you said the agreement of General Krstic was automatically implied. Now, was this the case always with -- I mean, in the chain of command that you accept, implied agreement, or is there any manifestation -- since he doesn't say no, he's supposed to be in agreement? Is this part of the system?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the chain of command was not broken globally speaking because the Srebrenica operation was underway; it continued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Was not broken. I mean, it was the discipline of the army and the orders had to pass through the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Generally speaking, commanders in the field always received orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes. In the case of this implicit -- this automatic agreement of General Krstic, he could have said "no."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rules allow it, but then he would have to be prepared to bear the consequences of such a response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And in your army, what were the consequences?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no such experience with such cases, but he would have had to explain why he was against it, why he was saying "no." He would have had to say, "No, I disagree, and I have a different proposal."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes. Of course I'm speaking of in case of the interest, in the interest of his mission. I'm not speaking of mutiny, of course. If someone doesn't want to execute an order because he doesn't feel it is the right one, he's entitled to reject it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is entitled to refuse and explain why he is refusing that order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Witness DB, I would like again to reiterate my thanks to you. You have cooperated with us. You said that the fatigue has taken its toll on you, but I think it has taken its toll more on the other people. You were very cooperative. And I would like to thank all those who really have been enduring this long trial today, but we had to do it so you can go back home safely. Thank you very much. We have admission of documents. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Riad. Let me express my thanks, too, to the staff who worked late and to Witness DB for enduring the cross-examination. If I could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You even owe him an apology, I think. Not to the Judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, I appreciate the patience of the witness, thank you. Let me move for admission, then, the following exhibits: Prosecutor's Exhibit 145/2 which was the slow-motion video. Prosecutor Exhibits 764/4 through 764/20A and B, those are the receipts from the Fontana Hotel.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, and C.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And C, where appropriate. 765 and 765A and B, the Zepa film and the transcript. 776A and B, which is the Krivaja 95 communications order. 784A and B, which is the -- this is the VRS communications manual. 785, which is a map. 819/1, 819/2, and 820, which are video stills taken from the film at Zepa. 821A and B, which is the Vukovic report dated 19 April. 822A and B which is -- we're moving to admit under seal, is a Drina Corps order dated the 19th of April, 1994. 823A and B, a Drina Corps order dated the 2nd of November, 1994. 824A and B, which is a Bratunac Brigade deployment order dated the 4th of June, 1995. 825A and B we're moving to admit under seal. It is the article that was testified about. 826 is -- I'm sorry, 826 is a still from a video showing a man in a black uniform with a radio pack on his back. 827A and B is an intelligence report from the East Bosnia Corps command dated the 23rd of July, 1995. 830A and B and 831A and B, these are documents that were provided by the Defence on 18 February 2000. Respectively, they are an 11 July order; there are two 11 July orders. And those are the exhibits that were tendered by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Just in passing, there is a mention here of Judge Rodrigues, and I just want to say that he is not present today, but he'll be present next time. So I don't know why they mention his name here, just before the end of the page. So I just want to draw that attention. Mr. Petrusic, do you have any comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence has no objection, but we would like to request a clarification from Mr. Harmon regarding Exhibit 765. That is the video film. Is that also part of the material seized or obtained from Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I am not in a position to give you an answer at this point the source of that film. I can reserve my application for admission of that exhibit, and then I can provide the Trial Chamber with further information when we're --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So with the exception of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, with the exception of the film, and then that would affect the film and the transcript which would be Exhibit 765 and 765A and B. We would withdraw our application for admission at this time and move to admit them at a later time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Is this satisfactory, Mr. Petrusic, his answer? Good, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: It is admitted with the exception of what you mentioned. I bring this trial today to an end, and thank you again. Yes, Mr. Petrusic. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No translation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You have to speak in English, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I think the interpreters have abandoned their posts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: They are entitled to. Can you say it in English, Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters are here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you hear the interpretation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Say it again then, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the examination of this witness, the Defence did not have exhibits, so we do not move for the introduction of any exhibits, for the admission of any exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.
